t.85: the boat belonged to some needy people who made their living from the sea and I damaged it because I knew that coming after them was a king who was seizing every [serviceable] boat by force.
t.95: As for the boat it belonged to some poor people who worked on the river, and I desired to damage it for beyond them lay the dominion of a king who was wont to seize every boat by force.
t.19: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the river, and I wished to mar it, for there was a king behind them who is taking every ship by force.
t.22: "As for the boat, it belonged to certain men in dire want: they plied on the water: I but wished to render it unserviceable, for there was after them a certain king who seized on every boat by force.
t.203: "As for the ship, it belonged to Masâkîn (poor people) working in the sea. So I wished to make a defective damage in it, as there was a king behind them who seized every ship by force.
t.54: کشتی تو چند مسکینوں کی تھی جو دریا میں کام کاج کرتے تھے۔ میں نے اس میں کچھ توڑ پھوڑ کرنے کا اراده کر لیا کیونکہ ان کے آگے ایک بادشاه تھا جو ہر ایک (صحیح سالم) کشتی کو جبراً ضبط کر لیتا تھا.

t.149: And as for the boy, his parents were believers and we feared he would overwhelm them with transgression and denial.
t.84: As for the boy, his parents were believers. We apprehended that he would impose rebellion and infidelity upon them.
t.85: The young boy had parents who were people of faith, and so, fearing he would trouble them through wickedness and disbelief,
t.95: As for the lad, his parents were people of faith, and we feared lest he should plague them with transgression and disbelief,
t.19: And as for the lad, his parents were believers and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.
t.22: "As for the youth, his parents were people of Faith, and we feared that he would grieve them by obstinate rebellion and ingratitude (to Allah and man).
t.203: "And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.
t.54: اور اس لڑکے کے ماں باپ ایمان والے تھے۔ ہمیں خوف ہوا کہ کہیں یہ انہیں اپنی سرکشی اور کفر سے عاجز وپریشان نہ کر دے.

t.149: So we wanted their Lord to replace him with someone of better purity and nearer to mercy.
t.84: We, therefore, wished that their Lord would replace him with someone better than him in piety, and more akin to affection.
t.85: we wished that their Lord should give them another child- purer and more compassionate- in his place.
t.95: and we desired that their Lord should grant them another in his place, a son more upright and more tender hearted.
t.19: And we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in purity and nearer to mercy.
t.22: "So we desired that their Lord would give them in exchange (a son) better in purity (of conduct) and closer in affection.
t.203: "So we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in righteousness and nearer to mercy.
t.54: اس لئے ہم نے چاہا کہ انہیں ان کا پروردگار اس کے بدلے اس سے بہتر پاکیزگی واﻻ اور اس سے زیاده محبت اور پیار واﻻ بچہ عنایت فرمائے.

t.149: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphaned boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure that belonged to them, and their father was a righteous man, so your Lord desired that they attain their full strength and(then) extract their treasure—a mercy from your Lord. And I never did it of my own accord. This is the interpretation of what you were unable to endure patiently.”
t.84: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was a treasure beneath it belonging to them, and their father was a pious man. So your Lord willed that they should reach their maturity and dig out their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it on my own accord. This is the reality of things about which you could not remain patient.”
t.85: The wall belonged to two young orphans in the town and there was buried treasure beneath it belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man, so your Lord intended them to reach maturity and then dig up their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do [these things] of my own accord: these are the explanations for those things you could not bear with patience.’
t.95: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and under it there was a treasure that belonged to them. Their father was a righteous man and your Lord intended that they should come of age and then bring forth their treasure as a mercy from your Lord; I did not do this of my own bidding. This is the true meaning of things with which you could not keep your patience."
t.19: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous, and thy Lord intended that they should come to their full strength and should bring forth their treasure as a mercy from their Lord; and I did it not upon my own command. Such is the interpretation of that wherewith thou couldst not bear.
t.22: "As for the wall, it belonged to two youths, orphans, in the Town; there was, beneath it, a buried treasure, to which they were entitled: their father had been a righteous man: So thy Lord desired that they should attain their age of full strength and get out their treasure - a mercy (and favour) from thy Lord. I did it not of my own accord. Such is the interpretation of (those things) over which thou wast unable to hold patience."
t.203: "And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town; and there was under it a treasure belonging to them; and their father was a righteous man, and your Lord intended that they should attain their age of full strength and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did them not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of those (things) over which you could not hold patience."
t.54: دیوار کا قصہ یہ ہے کہ اس شہر میں دو یتیم بچے ہیں جن کا خزانہ ان کی اس دیوار کے نیچے دفن ہے، ان کا باپ بڑا نیک شخص تھا تو تیرے رب کی چاہت تھی کہ یہ دونوں یتیم اپنی جوانی کی عمر میں آکر اپنا یہ خزانہ تیرے رب کی مہربانی اور رحمت سے نکال لیں، میں نے اپنی رائے سے کوئی کام نہیں کیا، یہ تھی اصل حقیقت ان واقعات کی جن پر آپ سے صبر نہ ہو سکا.

t.149: And they ask youabout Zul-Qarnayn. Say, “I will read for you an account of him as a reminder.”
t.84: They ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say, “I shall now recite to you an account of him.”
t.85: [Prophet], they ask you about Dhu ’l-Qarnayn. Say, ‘I will tell you something about him.’
t.95: (O Muhammad), they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: "I will give you an account of him."
t.19: They will ask thee of Dhu'l-Qarneyn. Say: I shall recite unto you a remembrance of him.
t.22: They ask thee concerning Zul-qarnain. Say, "I will rehearse to you something of his story."
t.203: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say: "I shall recite to you something of his story."
t.54: آپ سے ذوالقرنین کا واقعہ یہ لوگ دریافت کر رہے ہیں، آپ کہہ دیجئے کہ میں ان کا تھوڑا سا حال تمہیں پڑھ کر سناتا ہوں.

t.149: Indeed, We empowered him in the land and brought him all kinds of means.
t.84: Surely, We gave him power on earth and gave him means to (have) everything (he needs).
t.85: We established his power in the land, and gave him the means to achieve everything.
t.95: We granted him power in the land and endowed him with all kinds of resources.
t.19: Lo! We made him strong in the land and gave him unto every thing a road.
t.22: Verily We established his power on earth, and We gave him the ways and the means to all ends.
t.203: Verily, We established him in the earth, and We gave him the means of everything.
t.54: ہم نے اسے زمین میں قوت عطا فرمائی تھی اور اسے ہر چیز کے سامان بھی عنایت کردیے تھے.

t.149: So he pursued a certain course
t.84: So he followed a course,
t.85: He travelled on a certain road;
t.95: He set out (westwards) on an expedition,
t.19: And he followed a road
t.22: One (such) way he followed,
t.203: So he followed a way.
t.54: وه ایک راه کے پیچھے لگا.

t.149: until, when he had reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring, and found a people in its vicinity. We said, “O Zul-Qarnayn, you may either punish or else treat them kindly.”
t.84: until when he reached the point of sunset, he found it setting into a miry spring, and found a people near it. We said, “O Dhul-Qarnain, either punish them or adopt good behavior with them.”
t.85: then, when he came to the setting of the sun, he found it [seemed to be] setting into a muddy spring. Nearby he found some people and We said, ‘Dhu ’l-Qarnayn, you may choose [which of them] to punish or show kindness to.’
t.95: until when he reached the very limits where the sun sets, he saw it setting in dark turbid waters; and nearby he met a people. We said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, you have the power to punish or to treat them with kindness."
t.19: Till, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found a people thereabout. We said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Either punish or show them kindness.
t.22: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it set in a spring of murky water: Near it he found a People: We said: "O Zul-qarnain! (thou hast authority,) either to punish them, or to treat them with kindness."
t.203: Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of black muddy (or hot) water. And he found near it a people. We (Allâh) said (by inspiration): "O Dhul-Qarnain! Either you punish them, or treat them with kindness."
t.54: یہاں تک کہ سورج ڈوبنے کی جگہ پہنچ گیا اور اسے ایک دلدل کےچشمے میں غروب ہوتا ہوا پایا اور اس چشمے کے پاس ایک قوم کو بھی پایا، ہم نے فرما دیا کہ اے ذوالقرنین! یا تو تو انہیں تکلیف پہنچائے یا ان کے بارے میں تو کوئی بہترین روش اختیار کرے.

t.149: He said, “As for the one who has committed injustices, we will punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord and He will punish him with a dreadful punishment.
t.84: He said, “As for him who does wrong, we shall punish him, then he will be sent back to his Lord, and He will punish him with a severe punishment.
t.85: He answered, ‘We shall punish those who have done evil, and when they are returned to their Lord He will punish them [even more] severely,
t.95: He said: "We will chastise him who does wrong, whereafter he will be returned to his Lord and He will chastise him grievously.
t.19: He said: As for him who doeth wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with awful punishment!
t.22: He said: "Whoever doth wrong, him shall we punish; then shall he be sent back to his Lord; and He will punish him with a punishment unheard-of (before).
t.203: He said: "As for him (a disbeliever in the Oneness of Allâh) who does wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with a terrible torment (Hell).
t.54: اس نے کہا کہ جو ﻇلم کرے گا اسے تو ہم بھی اب سزا دیں گے، پھر وه اپنے پروردگار کی طرف لوٹایا جائے گا اور وه اسے سخت تر عذاب دے گا.

t.149: But as for the one who has attained faith and has acted righteously, then for him is the excellent(reward) as repayment , and we will speak to him with ease regarding our command.”
t.84: As for the one who believes and acts righteously, he will have the best (life) as reward, and we shall speak to him politely in our directions.”
t.85: while those who believed and did good deeds will have the best of rewards: we shall command them to do what is easy for them.’
t.95: But as for him who believes and acts righteously, his will be a goodly reward and we shall enjoin upon him only mild commands."
t.19: But as for him who believeth and doeth right, good will be his reward, and We shall speak unto him a mild command.
t.22: "But whoever believes, and works righteousness,- he shall have a goodly reward, and easy will be his task as We order it by our Command."
t.203: "But as for him who believes (in Allâh’s Oneness) and works righteousness, he shall have the best reward, (Paradise), and we (Dhul-Qarnain) shall speak unto him mild words (as instructions)."
t.54: ہاں جو ایمان ﻻئے اور نیک اعمال کرے اس کے لئے تو بدلے میں بھلائی ہے اور ہم اسے اپنے کام میں بھی آسانی ہی کا حکم دیں گے.

t.149: Then he pursued a course
t.84: Thereafter, he followed a course,
t.85: He travelled on;
t.95: Then he set out on another expedition
t.19: Then he followed a road
t.22: Then followed he (another) way,
t.203: Then he followed another way,
t.54: پھر وه اور راه کے پیچھے لگا.

t.149: until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
t.84: until when he reached the point of sunrise, he found it rising over a people for whom We did not make any shelter against it.
t.85: then, when he came to the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
t.95: until he reached the limit where the sun rises and he found it rising on a people whom We had provided no shelter from it.
t.19: Till, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had appointed no shelter therefrom.
t.22: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no covering protection against the sun.
t.203: Until, when he came to the rising place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We (Allâh) had provided no shelter against the sun.
t.54: یہاں تک کہ جب سورج نکلنے کی جگہ تک پہنچا تو اسے ایک ایسی قوم پر نکلتا پایا کہ ان کے لئے ہم نے اس سے اور کوئی اوٹ نہیں بنائی.

t.149: So it was. And surely We encompassed what he had with knowledge.
t.84: Thus it was, and Our knowledge fully comprehends whatever (wealth and equipment) he had with him.
t.85: And so it was: We knew all about him.
t.95: Thus was the state of those people, and We encompassed in knowledge all concerning Dhu al- Qarnayn.
t.19: So (it was). And We knew all concerning him.
t.22: (He left them) as they were: We completely understood what was before him.
t.203: So (it was)! And We knew all about him (Dhul-Qarnain).
t.54: واقعہ ایسا ہی ہے اور ہم نے اس کے پاس کی کل خبروں کا احاطہ کر رکھا ہے.

t.149: Then he pursued a course
t.84: Thereafter he followed a course
t.85: He travelled on;
t.95: Then he set out on another expedition
t.19: Then he followed a road
t.22: Then followed he (another) way,
t.203: Then he followed (another) way,
t.54: وه پھر ایک سفر کے سامان میں لگا.

t.149: until, when he reached the point separating the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely comprehend any word.
t.84: until when he reached between the two mountains, he found by them a people who were almost unable to understand anything said.
t.85: then, when he reached a place between two mountain barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely understand him.
t.95: until when he reached a place between the two mountains, he found beside the mountains a people who scarcely understood anything.
t.19: Till, when he came between the two mountains, he found upon their hither side a folk that scarce could understand a saying.
t.22: Until, when he reached (a tract) between two mountains, he found, beneath them, a people who scarcely understood a word.
t.203: Until, when he reached between two mountains, he found, before (near) them (those two mountains), a people who scarcely understood a word.
t.54: یہاں تک کہ جب دو دیواروں کے درمیان پہنچا ان دونوں کے پرے اس نے ایک ایسی قوم پائی جو بات سمجھنے کے قریب بھی نہ تھی.

t.149: They said, “O Zul-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are corrupting the land, so can we make for you a tribute on condition that you build a barrier between us and them?”
t.84: They said, “O Dhul-Qarnain, the (tribes of) Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj (Gog and Magog) are mischief-makers on the earth. So, should we assign a tax for you on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?”
t.85: They said, ‘Dhu ’l-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are ruining this land. Will you build a barrier between them and us if we pay you a tribute?’
t.95: They said: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are spreading corruption in this land. So shall we pay you taxes on the understanding that you will set up a barrier between us and them?"
t.19: They said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Lo! Gog and Magog are spoiling the land. So may we pay thee tribute on condition that thou set a barrier between us and them?
t.22: They said: "O Zul-qarnain! the Gog and Magog (People) do great mischief on earth: shall we then render thee tribute in order that thou mightest erect a barrier between us and them?
t.203: They said: "O Dhul-Qarnain! Verily Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog) are doing great mischief in the land. Shall we then pay you a tribute in order that you might erect a barrier between us and them?"
t.54: انہوں نے کہا اے ذوالقرنین! یاجوج ماجوج اس ملک میں (بڑے بھاری) فسادی ہیں، تو کیا ہم آپ کے لئے کچھ خرچ کا انتظام کر دیں؟ (اس شرط پر کہ) آپ ہمارے اور ان کے درمیان ایک دیوار بنادیں.

t.149: He said, “What my Lord has empowered me with is better.(Just) assist me with(man) power, and I will set a barricade between youand them.
t.84: He said, “What my Lord has (already) given in my control is better enough (for me than the tax you are offering to me), so help me (only) with some (man) power, and I shall make a rampart between you and them.
t.85: He answered, ‘The power my Lord has given me is better than any tribute, but if you lend me your strength, I will put up a fortification between you and them:
t.95: He answered: "Whatever my Lord has granted me is good enough. But help me with your labour and I will erect a rampart between you and them.
t.19: He said: That wherein my Lord hath established me is better (than your tribute). Do but help me with strength (of men), I will set between you and them a bank.
t.22: He said: "(The power) in which my Lord has established me is better (than tribute): Help me therefore with strength (and labour): I will erect a strong barrier between you and them:
t.203: He said: "That (wealth, authority and power) in which my Lord had established me is better (than your tribute). So help me with strength (of men), I will erect between you and them a barrier.
t.54: اس نے جواب دیا کہ میرے اختیار میں میرے پروردگار نے جو دے رکھا ہے وہی بہتر ہے، تم صرف قوت طاقت سے میری مدد کرو. میں تم میں اور ان میں مضبوط حجاب بنا دیتا ہوں

t.149: Bring me blocks of iron.” Then when he had leveled up between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow.” And having turned it into a fire, he said, “Bring me tar to pour over it.”
t.84: Bring me big pieces of iron.” (They proceeded accordingly) until when he leveled up (the gap) between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow.” (They complied) until when he made it (like) fire, he said, “Bring me molten copper, and I will pour it upon this.”
t.85: bring me lumps of iron!’ and then, when he had filled the gap between the two mountainsides [he said], ‘Work your bellows!’ and then, when he had made it glow like fire, he said, ‘Bring me molten metal to pour over it!’
t.95: Bring me ingots of iron." Then after he had filled up the space between the two mountain-sides, he said: "(Light a fire) and ply bellows." When he had made it (red like) fire, he said: "Bring me molten copper which I may pour on it."
t.19: Give me pieces of iron - till, when he had levelled up (the gap) between the cliffs, he said: Blow! - till, when he had made it a fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour thereon.
t.22: "Bring me blocks of iron." At length, when he had filled up the space between the two steep mountain-sides, He said, "Blow (with your bellows)" Then, when he had made it (red) as fire, he said: "Bring me, that I may pour over it, molten lead."
t.203: "Give me pieces (blocks) of iron;" then, when he had filled up the gap between the two mountain-cliffs, he said: "Blow;" then when he had made them (red as) fire, he said: "Bring me molten copper to pour over them."
t.54: مجھے لوہے کی چادریں ﻻ دو۔ یہاں تک کہ جب ان دونوں پہاڑوں کے درمیان دیوار برابر کر دی تو حکم دیا کہ آگ تیز جلاؤ تاوقتیکہ لوہے کی ان چادروں کو بالکل آگ کر دیا، تو فرمایا میرے پاس ﻻؤ اس پر پگھلا ہوا تانبا ڈال دوں.

t.149: So neither could they climb it, nor could they penetrate it.
t.84: So they (Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj) were not able to climb it, nor were they able to make a hole in it.
t.85: Their enemies could not scale the barrier, nor could they pierce it,
t.95: Such was the rampart that Gog and Magog could not scale, nor could they pierce it.
t.19: And (Gog and Magog) were not able to surmount, nor could they pierce (it).
t.22: Thus were they made powerless to scale it or to dig through it.
t.203: So they [Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog)] could not scale it or dig through it.
t.54: پس تو ان میں اس دیوار کے اوپر چڑھنے کی طاقت تھی اور نہ ان میں کوئی سوراخ کر سکتے تھے.

t.149: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes true, He will turn it into a flat surface . And the promise of my Lord has always been true.”
t.84: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord. Then, when the promise of my Lord will come, He will make it leveled to the ground. The promise of my Lord is true.”
t.85: and he said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord. But when my Lord’s promise is fulfilled, He will raze this barrier to the ground: my Lord’s promise always comes true.’
t.95: Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "This is a mercy from my Lord: but when the time of my Lord's promise shall come, He will level the rampart with the ground. My Lord's promise always comes true."
t.19: He said: This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord cometh to pass, He will lay it low, for the promise of my Lord is true.
t.22: He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord: But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it into dust; and the promise of my Lord is true."
t.203: (Dhul-Qarnain) said: "This is a mercy from my Lord, but when the Promise of my Lord comes, He shall level it down to the ground. And the Promise of my Lord is ever true."
t.54: کہا یہ صرف میرے رب کی مہربانی ہے ہاں جب میرے رب کا وعده آئے گا تو اسے زمین بوس کر دے گا، بیشک میرے رب کا وعده سچا اور حق ہے.

t.149: And We leftthem surging upon one another on that day, and the Trumpet was blown and We gathered them together.
t.84: And on that day, (i.e. the Doomsday) We will leave them (all the people including Ya’jūj and Ma’jūj) surging over one another. And the Horn shall be blown, then We shall gather them together.
t.85: On that Day, We shall let them surge against each other like waves and then the Trumpet will be blown and We shall gather them all together.
t.95: And on that Day We shall let some of them surge like waves against others, and the Trumpet shall be blown. Then We shall gather them all together.
t.19: And on that day we shall let some of them surge against others, and the Trumpet will be blown. Then We shall gather them together in one gathering.
t.22: On that day We shall leave them to surge like waves on one another: the trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them all together.
t.203: And on that Day [i.e. the Day Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog) will come out], We shall leave them to surge like waves on one another; and the Trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them (the creatures) all together.
t.54: اس دن ہم انہیں آپس میں ایک دوسرے میں گڈ مڈ ہوتے ہوئے چھوڑ دیں گے اور صور پھونک دیا جائے گا پس سب کو اکٹھا کرکے ہم جمع کر لیں گے.

t.149: And We displayed Hell to the deniers on that day in full display—
t.84: And on that day We will bring Jahannam fully exposed before the infidels
t.85: We shall show Hell to the disbelievers,
t.95: That will be the Day We shall place Hell before the unbelievers
t.19: On that day we shall present hell to the disbelievers, plain to view,
t.22: And We shall present Hell that day for Unbelievers to see, all spread out,-
t.203: And on that Day We shall present Hell to the disbelievers, plain to view -
t.54: اس دن ہم جہنم کو (بھی) کافروں کے سامنے ﻻکھڑا کر دیں گے.

t.149: those whose eyes were covered from My Reminder and were unable to hear.
t.84: whose eyes were under a cover against My reminders, and they were not able to listen.
t.85: those whose eyes were blind to My signs, those who were unable to hear.
t.95: whose eyes had become blind against My admonition and who were utterly disinclined to hear it.
t.19: Those whose eyes were hoodwinked from My reminder, and who could not bear to hear.
t.22: (Unbelievers) whose eyes had been under a veil from remembrance of Me, and who had been unable even to hear.
t.203: (To) those whose eyes had been under a covering from My Reminder (this Qur’ân), and who could not bear to hear (it).
t.54: جن کی آنکھیں میری یاد سے پردے میں تھی اور (امر حق) سن بھی نہیں سکتے تھے.

t.149: Did those who have denied think that they could take My servants for masters apart from Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the hospitality of the deniers.
t.84: Do, then, the disbelievers deem (it fit) that they take My servants as patrons beside Me? Surely, We have prepared Jahannam as entertainment for the disbelievers.
t.85: Did they think that they could take My servants as masters instead of Me? We have prepared Hell as the disbelievers’ resting place.
t.95: Do the unbelievers, then, believe that they can take any of My creatures as their guardians beside Me? Verily We have prepared Hell to welcome the unbelievers.
t.19: Do the disbelievers reckon that they can choose My bondmen as protecting friends beside Me? Lo! We have prepared hell as a welcome for the disbelievers.
t.22: Do the Unbelievers think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Verily We have prepared Hell for the Unbelievers for (their) entertainment.
t.203: Do then those who disbelieved think that they can take My slaves [i.e., the angels, Allâh’s Messengers, ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary)] as Auliyâ’ (lords, gods, protectors) besides Me? Verily, We have prepared Hell as an entertainment for the disbelievers (in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism).
t.54: کیا کافر یہ خیال کیے بیٹھے ہیں؟ کہ میرے سوا وه میرے بندوں کو اپنا حمایتی بنا لیں گے؟ (سنو) ہم نے تو ان کفار کی مہمانی کے لئے جہنم کو تیار کر رکھا ہے.

t.149: Say, “Shall We inform youof the biggest losers regarding deeds?
t.84: Say, “Shall We tell you about the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds?
t.85: Say [Prophet], ‘Shall we tell you who has the most to lose by their actions,
t.95: Say, (O Muhammad): "Shall We tell you who will be the greatest losers in respect of their works?
t.19: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers by their works?
t.22: Say: "Shall we tell you of those who lose most in respect of their deeds?-
t.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "Shall We tell you the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds?
t.54: کہہ دیجئے کہ اگر (تم کہو تو) میں تمہیں بتا دوں کہ باعتبار اعمال سب سے زیاده خسارے میں کون ہیں؟

t.149: Those whose efforts in the Earlier Life have gone astray, while they assume that they are doing well.”
t.84: Those are the ones whose effort in the worldly life has gone in vain, while they think they are doing well.
t.85: whose efforts in this world are misguided, even when they think they are doing good work?
t.95: It will be those whose effort went astray in the life of the world and who believe nevertheless that they are doing good.
t.19: Those whose effort goeth astray in the life of the world, and yet they reckon that they do good work.
t.22: "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life, while they thought that they were acquiring good by their works?"
t.203: "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life while they thought that they were acquiring good by their deeds.
t.54: وه ہیں کہ جن کی دنیوی زندگی کی تمام تر کوششیں بیکار ہوگئیں اور وه اسی گمان میں رہے کہ وه بہت اچھے کام کر رہے ہیں.

t.149: Those are the ones who denied the signs of their Lord and the meeting with Him, so their deeds were nullified, and on the Day of Resurrection We will consider them of no weight.
t.84: Those are the ones who rejected the signs of their Lord and (the concept of) meeting with Him, so their deeds have gone to waste, and We shall assign to them no weight at all.
t.85: It is those who disbelieve in their Lord’s messages and deny that they will meet Him.’ Their deeds come to nothing: on the Day of Resurrection We shall give them no weight.
t.95: Those are the ones who refused to believe in the revelations of their Lord and that they are bound to meet Him. Hence, all their deeds have come to naught, and We shall assign no weight to them on the Day of Resurrection.
t.19: Those are they who disbelieve in the revelations of their Lord and in the meeting with Him. Therefor their works are vain, and on the Day of Resurrection We assign no weight to them.
t.22: They are those who deny the Signs of their Lord and the fact of their having to meet Him (in the Hereafter): vain will be their works, nor shall We, on the Day of Judgment, give them any weight.
t.203: "They are those who deny the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of their Lord and the Meeting with Him (in the Hereafter). So their works are in vain, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall assign no weight for them.
t.54: یہی وه لوگ ہیں جنہوں نے اپنے پروردگار کی آیتوں اور اس کی ملاقات سے کفر کیا، اس لئے ان کے اعمال غارت ہوگئے پس قیامت کے دن ہم ان کا کوئی وزن قائم نہ کریں گے.

t.149: That is their repayment—Hell—on account of their denial and their taking My signs and My messengers in mockery.
t.84: That is their punishment, the Jahannam , for they disbelieved and made My signs and My messengers a mockery.
t.85: Their recompense for having disbelieved and made fun of My messages and My messengers will be Hell.
t.95: Hell is their recompense for disbelieving and their taking My revelations and My Messengers as objects of jest.
t.19: That is their reward: hell, because they disbelieved, and made a jest of Our revelations and Our messengers.
t.22: That is their reward, Hell, because they rejected Faith, and took My Signs and My Messengers by way of jest.
t.203: "That shall be their recompense, Hell; because they disbelieved and took My Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) and My Messengers by way of jest and mockery.
t.54: حال یہ ہے کہ ان کا بدلہ جہنم ہے کیونکہ انہوں نے کفر کیا اور میری آیتوں اور میرے رسولوں کو مذاق میں اڑایا.

t.149: Indeed, those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds—the Gardens of Paradise have always been there for their hospitality,
t.84: Surely those who believed and did righteous deeds, theirs are the Gardens of Firdaus as entertainment
t.85: But those who believe and do good deeds will be given the Gardens of Paradise.
t.95: As for those who believe and do good works, the Gardens of Paradise shall be there to welcome them;
t.19: Lo! those who believe and do good works, theirs are the Gardens of Paradise for welcome,
t.22: As to those who believe and work righteous deeds, they have, for their entertainment, the Gardens of Paradise,
t.203: "Verily those who believe (in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism) and do righteous deeds, shall have the Gardens of Al-Firdaus (Paradise) for their entertainment.
t.54: جو لوگ ایمان ﻻئے اور انہوں نے کام بھی اچھے کیے یقیناً ان کے لئے الفردوس کے باغات کی مہمانی ہے.

t.149: abiding therein, never seeking to leave it.
t.84: where they will live forever, and will not wish to move from there.”
t.85: There they will remain, never wishing to leave.
t.95: there they will abide for ever, with no desire to be removed from there."
t.19: Wherein they will abide, with no desire to be removed from thence.
t.22: Wherein they shall dwell (for aye): no change will they wish for from them.
t.203: "Wherein they shall dwell (forever). No desire will they have for removal therefrom."
t.54: جہاں وه ہمیشہ رہا کریں گے جس جگہ کو بدلنے کا کبھی بھی ان کا اراده ہی نہ ہوگا.

t.149: Say, “If the sea were to become ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would run out before the words of my Lord ran out, even if We were to bring the like of it in replenishment.”
t.84: Say, “If the ocean were to be ink for (writing) the Words of my Lord, the ocean would have been consumed before the Words of my Lord are exhausted, even though we were to bring another (ocean) like it in addition.”
t.85: Say [Prophet], ‘If the whole ocean were ink for writing the words of my Lord, it would run dry before those words were exhausted’- even if We were to add another ocean to it.
t.95: Say: "If the sea were to become ink to record the Words of my Lord, indeed the sea would be all used up before the Words of my Lord are exhausted, and it would be the same even if We were to bring an equal amount of ink."
t.19: Say: Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though We brought the like thereof to help.
t.22: Say: "If the ocean were ink (wherewith to write out) the words of my Lord, sooner would the ocean be exhausted than would the words of my Lord, even if we added another ocean like it, for its aid."
t.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم to mankind): "If the sea were ink for (writing) the Words of my Lord, surely, the sea would be exhausted before the Words of my Lord would be finished, even if We brought (another sea) like it for its aid."
t.54: کہہ دیجئے کہ اگر میرے پروردگار کی باتوں کے لکھنے کے لئے سمندر سیاہی بن جائے تو وه بھی میرے رب کی باتوں کے ختم ہونے سے پہلے ہی ختم ہو جائے گا، گو ہم اسی جیسا اور بھی اس کی مدد میں لے آئیں.

t.149: Say, “Indeed, I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your god is One God, so whoever expects to meet his Lord, let him do righteous work and never associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
t.84: Say, “Surely, I am but a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is the One God. So the one who hopes to meet his Lord must do righteous deed and must not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
t.85: Say, ‘I am only a human being, like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is One. Anyone who fears to meet his Lord should do good deeds and give no one a share in the worship due to his Lord.
t.95: Say (O Muhammad): "I am no more than a human being like you; one to whom revelation is made: 'Your Lord is the One and Only God.' Hence, whoever looks forward to meet his Lord, let him do righteous works, and let him associate none with the worship of his Lord."
t.19: Say: I am only a mortal like you. My Lord inspireth in me that your Allah is only One Allah. And whoever hopeth for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work, and make none sharer of the worship due unto his Lord.
t.22: Say: "I am but a man like yourselves, (but) the inspiration has come to me, that your Allah is one Allah: whoever expects to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness, and, in the worship of his Lord, admit no one as partner.
t.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your Ilâh (God) is One Ilâh (God - i.e. Allâh). So whoever hopes for the Meeting with his Lord, let him work righteousness and associate none as a partner in the worship of his Lord."
t.54: آپ کہہ دیجئے کہ میں تو تم جیسا ہی ایک انسان ہوں- (ہاں) میری جانب وحی کی جاتی ہے کہ سب کا معبود صرف ایک ہی معبود ہے، تو جسے بھی اپنے پروردگار سے ملنے کی آرزو ہو اسے چاہئے کہ نیک اعمال کرے اور اپنے پروردگار کی عبادت میں کسی کو بھی شریک نہ کرے.

t.149: Kāf, Hā Yā, ‘Ain, Sād.
t.84: Kāf, Hā Yā, ‘Ain, Sād
t.85: Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad
t.95: Kaf. Ha'. Ya'. Ayn. Sad.
t.19: Kaf. Ha. Ya. A'in. Sad.
t.22: Kaf. Ha. Ya. 'Ain. Sad.
t.203: Kâf-Hâ-Yâ-‘Aîn-Sâd. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ân, and none but Allâh (Alone) knows their meanings].
t.54: کہیعص.*

t.149: A reminder of yourLord’s mercy towards His servant Zechariah,
t.84: This is a narration of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zakariyyā,
t.85: This is an account of your Lord’s grace towards His servant, Zachariah,
t.95: This is an account of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
t.19: A mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah.
t.22: (This is) a recital of the Mercy of thy Lord to His servant Zakariya.
t.203: (This is) a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His slave Zakariyyâ (Zachariah).
t.54: یہ ہے تیرے پروردگار کی اس مہربانی کا ذکر جو اس نے اپنے بندے زکریا پر کی تھی.

t.149: when he called out to his Lord a call in seclusion.
t.84: When he called his Lord in a low voice.
t.85: when he called to his Lord secretly, saying,
t.95: when he cried to his Lord in secret.
t.19: When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret,
t.22: Behold! he cried to his Lord in secret,
t.203: When he called out his Lord (Allâh) a call in secret.
t.54: جبکہ اس نے اپنے رب سے چپکے چپکے دعا کی تھی.

t.149: He said, “My Lord, my bones have become feeble and my hair is aflame with gray, and never, in calling upon You my Lord, have I been wretched.
t.84: He said, “My Lord, I am in a state that bones in my body have turned feeble, and the head has flared up grey with old age, and I never remained, My Lord, unanswered in my prayer to You.
t.85: ‘Lord, my bones have weakened and my hair is ashen grey, but never, Lord, have I ever prayed to You in vain:
t.95: He said: "Lord! My bones have grown feeble and my head is glistening with age; yet, never have my prayers to You, my Lord, been unfruitful.
t.19: Saying: My Lord! Lo! the bones of me wax feeble and my head is shining with grey hair, and I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord.
t.22: Praying: "O my Lord! infirm indeed are my bones, and the hair of my head doth glisten with grey: but never am I unblest, O my Lord, in my prayer to Thee!
t.203: He said: "My Lord! Indeed my bones have grown feeble, and grey hair has spread on my head, And I have never been unblest in my invocation to You, O my Lord!
t.54: کہ اے میرے پروردگار! میری ہڈیاں کمزور ہوگئی ہیں اور سر بڑھاپے کی وجہ سے بھڑک اٹھا ہے، لیکن میں کبھی بھی تجھ سے دعا کر کے محروم نہیں رہا.

t.149: And indeed, I am afraid of what my protégés will do when I am gone, for my wife has always been barren. So grant me from Yourself a guardian
t.84: I fear (my) kinsmen after me, and my wife is barren, so bless me with an heir, from Your own side,
t.85: I fear [what] my kinsmen [will do] when I am gone, for my wife is barren, so grant me a successor––a gift from You––
t.95: I fear evil from my kinsmen after I am gone; and my wife is barren, so grant me an heir out of Your special grace,
t.19: Lo! I fear my kinsfolk after me, since my wife is barren. Oh, give me from Thy presence a successor
t.22: "Now I fear (what) my relatives (and colleagues) (will do) after me: but my wife is barren: so give me an heir as from Thyself,-
t.203: "And verily I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren. So give me from Yourself an heir.
t.54: مجھے اپنے مرنے کے بعد اپنے قرابت والوں کا ڈر ہے، میری بیوی بھی بانجھ ہے پس تو مجھے اپنے پاس سے وارث عطا فرم.

t.149: to inherit from me and inherit from Jacob’s folk, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.”
t.84: who inherits me and inherits the house of Ya‘qūb. And make him, My Lord, a favourite one.”
t.85: to be my heir and the heir of the family of Jacob. Lord, make him well pleasing [to You].’
t.95: one that might be my heir and the heir of the house of Jacob; and make him, Lord, one that will be pleasing to You.
t.19: Who shall inherit of me and inherit (also) of the house of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, acceptable (unto Thee).
t.22: "(One that) will (truly) represent me, and represent the posterity of Jacob; and make him, O my Lord! one with whom Thou art well-pleased!"
t.203: "Who shall inherit me, and inherit (also) the posterity of Ya‘qûb (Jacob) (inheritance of the religious knowledge and Prophethood, not of wealth.). And make him, my Lord, one with whom You are Well-Pleased!"
t.54: جو میرا بھی وارث ہو اور یعقوب (علیہ السلام) کے خاندان کا بھی جانشین اور میرے رب! تو اسے مقبول بنده بنا لے.

t.149: “O Zechariah, indeed, We give you glad tidings of a boy whose name is John; We have never made anyone similar to himbefore.”
t.84: (Allah said) “O Zakariyyā, We give you the good news of a boy whose name is YaHyā. We did not create any one before him of the same name.”
t.85: ‘Zachariah, We bring you good news of a son whose name will be John––We have chosen this name for no one before him.’
t.95: (He was told): "Zechariah, We bring you the good news of the birth of a son whose name shall be Yahya (John), one whose namesake We never created before."
t.19: (It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him).
t.22: (His prayer was answered): "O Zakariya! We give thee good news of a son: His name shall be Yahya: on none by that name have We conferred distinction before."
t.203: (Allâh said) "O Zakariyyâ (Zachariah)! Verily, We give you the glad tidings of a son, whose name will be Yahyâ (John). We have given that name to none before (him)."
t.54: اے زکریا! ہم تجھے ایک بچے کی خوشخبری دیتے ہیں جس کا نام یحيٰ ہے، ہم نے اس سے پہلے اس کا ہم نام بھی کسی کو نہیں کیا.

t.149: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife has always been barren and I have become decrepit with old age?”
t.84: He Said, “My Lord, how shall there be a boy for me while my wife is barren, and I have reached the extreme of old age?”
t.85: He said, ‘Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren, and I am old and frail?’
t.95: He said: "My Lord! How can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached an extremely old age?"
t.19: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached infirm old age?
t.22: He said: "O my Lord! How shall I have a son, when my wife is barren and I have grown quite decrepit from old age?"
t.203: He said: "My Lord! How can I have a son, when my wife is barren, and I have reached the extreme old age."
t.54: زکریا (علیہ السلام) کہنے لگے میرے رب! میرے ہاں لڑکا کیسے ہوگا، جبکہ میری بیوی بانجھ اور میں خود بڑھاپے کے انتہائی ضعف کو پہنچ چکا ہوں.

t.149: He said, “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for Me, and I have certainly created youbefore when you were nothing.’”
t.84: He said, “So it is; your Lord said ‘it is easy for Me, and I did create you before, when you were nothing.’”
t.85: He said, ‘This is what your Lord has said: “It is easy for Me: I created you, though you were nothing before.” ’
t.95: He answered: "So shall it be." Your Lord says: "It is easy for Me," and then added: "For beyond doubt, I created you earlier when you were nothing."
t.19: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me, even as I created thee before, when thou wast naught.
t.22: He said: "So (it will be) thy Lord saith, 'that is easy for Me: I did indeed create thee before, when thou hadst been nothing!'"
t.203: He said: "So (it will be). Your Lord says: It is easy for Me. Certainly I have created you before, when you had been nothing!"
t.54: ارشاد ہوا کہ وعده اسی طرح ہو چکا، تیرے رب نے فرما دیا ہے کہ مجھ پر تو یہ بالکل آسان ہے اور تو خود جبکہ کچھ نہ تھا میں تجھے پیدا کر چکا ہوں.

t.149: He said, “My Lord, give me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you do not speak to people for three nights,(despite) being in perfect shape.”
t.84: He said, “My Lord, make for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not (be able to) speak to the people for three (consecutive) nights, even though you will be sound in health.”
t.85: He said, ‘Give me a sign, Lord.’ He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not [be able to] speak to anyone for three full [days and] nights.’
t.95: Zechariah said: "Lord, grant me a Sign." Said He: "Your Sign is that you shall not be able to speak to people for three nights, though you will be otherwise sound."
t.19: He said: My Lord! Appoint for me some token. He said: Thy token is that thou, with no bodily defect, shalt not speak unto mankind three nights.
t.22: (Zakariya) said: "O my Lord! give me a Sign." "Thy Sign," was the answer, "Shall be that thou shalt speak to no man for three nights, although thou art not dumb."
t.203: [Zakariyyâ (Zachariah)] said: "My Lord! Appoint for me a sign." He said: "Your sign is that you shall not speak unto mankind for three nights, though having no bodily defect."
t.54: کہنے لگے میرے پروردگار میرے لئے کوئی علامت مقرر فرما دے، ارشاد ہوا کہ تیرے لئے علامت یہ ہے کہ باوجود بھلا چنگا ہونے کے تو تین راتوں تک کسی شخص سے بول نہ سکے گا.

t.149: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary and signaled to them to exalt(God) , morning and evening.
t.84: Then he came out to his people from the place of prayer, and directed them by gestures to proclaim the purity of Allah at morning and evening.
t.85: He went out of the sanctuary to his people and signalled to them to praise God morning and evening.
t.95: Thereupon Zechariah came out from the sanctuary and directed his people by gestures to extol His glory by day and by night.
t.19: Then he came forth unto his people from the sanctuary, and signified to them: Glorify your Lord at break of day and fall of night.
t.22: So Zakariya came out to his people from him chamber: He told them by signs to celebrate Allah's praises in the morning and in the evening.
t.203: Then he came out to his people from Al-Mihrâb (a praying place or a private room), and he told them by signs to glorify Allâh’s Praises in the morning and in the afternoon.
t.54: اب زکریا (علیہ السلام) اپنے حجرے سے نکل کر اپنی قوم کے پاس آکر انہیں اشاره کرتے ہیں کہ تم صبح وشام اللہ تعالیٰ کی تسبیح بیان کرو.

t.149: “O John, hold on to the Scripture firmly,” and We gave him wise judgment in his youth
t.84: (When the child was born, Allah said to him,) “O YaHyā, hold on to the Book firmly.” And We gave him wisdom, while he was still a child,
t.85: [We said], ‘John, hold on to the Scripture firmly.’ While he was still a boy, We granted him wisdom,
t.95: "O John! Hold the Book with all your strength." We had bestowed wisdom upon him while he was still a child;
t.19: (And it was said unto his son): O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child,
t.22: (To his son came the command): "O Yahya! take hold of the Book with might": and We gave him Wisdom even as a youth,
t.203: (It was said to his son): "O Yahyâ (John)! Hold fast the Scripture [the Taurât (Torah)]." And We gave him wisdom while yet a child.
t.54: اے یحيٰ! میری کتابکو مضبوطی سے تھام لے اور ہم نے اسے لڑکپن ہی سے دانائی عطا فرما دی.

t.149: and tenderness from Us and purity, and he was mindful(of God) ,
t.84: and (blessed him with) love from our own, and purity; and he was God-fearing,
t.85: tenderness from Us, and purity. He was devout,
t.95: and We also endowed him with tenderness and purity, and he was exceedingly pious
t.19: And compassion from Our presence, and purity; and he was devout,
t.22: And piety (for all creatures) as from Us, and purity: He was devout,
t.203: And (made him) sympathetic to men as a mercy (or a grant) from Us, and pure from sins [i.e. Yahyâ (John)] and he was righteous,
t.54: اور اپنے پاس سے شفقت اور پاکیزگی بھی، وه پرہیزگار شخص تھا.

t.149: and was very kind to his parents, and he was never a disobedient coercer.
t.84: and he was good to his parents; and he was not oppressive (or) disobedient.
t.85: kind to his parents, not domineering or rebellious.
t.95: and cherishing to his parents. Never was he insolent or rebellious.
t.19: And dutiful toward his parents. And he was not arrogant, rebellious.
t.22: And kind to his parents, and he was not overbearing or rebellious.
t.203: And dutiful towards his parents, and he was neither arrogant nor disobedient (to Allâh or to his parents).
t.54: اور اپنے ماں باپ سے نیک سلوک کرنے واﻻ تھا وه سرکش اور گناه گار نہ تھا.

t.149: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is resurrected alive.
t.84: Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.
t.85: Peace was on him the day he was born, the day he died, and it will be on him the day he is raised to life again.
t.95: Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he will die, and the day he will be raised up alive.
t.19: Peace on him the day he was born, and the day he dieth and the day he shall be raised alive!
t.22: So Peace on him the day he was born, the day that he dies, and the day that he will be raised up to life (again)!
t.203: And Salâm (peace) be on him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he will be raised up to life (again)!
t.54: اس پر سلام ہے جس دن وه پیدا ہوا اور جس دن وه مرے اور جس دن وه زنده کرکے اٹھایا جائے.

t.149: And rememberin the Scripture Mary, when she secluded herself from her family in an eastern location.
t.84: And mention in the Book (the story of) Maryam, when she secluded herself from her people to a place towards East,
t.85: Mention in the Quran the story of Mary. She withdrew from her family to a place to the east
t.95: (O Muhammad), recite in the Book the account of Mary, when she withdrew from her people to a place towards the east;
t.19: And make mention of Mary in the Scripture, when she had withdrawn from her people to a chamber looking East,
t.22: Relate in the Book (the story of) Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the East.
t.203: And mention in the Book (the Qur’ân, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم the story of) Maryam (Mary), when she withdrew in seclusion from her family to a place facing east.
t.54: اس کتاب میں مریم کا بھی واقعہ بیان کر۔ جبکہ وه اپنے گھر کے لوگوں سے علیحده ہو کر مشرقی جانب آئیں.

t.149: And she took a cover for herself away from them, and We sent to her Our spirit, so He appeared to her as a human being in perfect shape.
t.84: then she used a barrier to hide herself from them. Then, We sent to her Our Spirit, (Jibra’īl) and he took before her the form of a perfect human being.
t.85: and secluded herself away; We sent Our Spirit to appear before her in the form of a perfected man.
t.95: and drew a curtain, screening herself from people whereupon We sent to her Our spirit and he appeared to her as a well-shaped man.
t.19: And had chosen seclusion from them. Then We sent unto her Our Spirit and it assumed for her the likeness of a perfect man.
t.22: She placed a screen (to screen herself) from them; then We sent her our angel, and he appeared before her as a man in all respects.
t.203: She placed a screen (to screen herself) from them; then We sent to her Our Ruh [angel Jibrîl (Gabriel)], and he appeared before her in the form of a man in all respects.
t.54: اور ان لوگوں کی طرف سے پرده کر لیا، پھر ہم نے اس کے پاس اپنی روح (جبرائیل علیہ السلام) کو بھیجا پس وه اس کے سامنے پورا آدمی بن کر ﻇاہر ہوا.

t.149: She said, “I seek refuge from you with the All-Merciful, if you are mindful(of God) .”
t.84: She said, “I seek refuge with the All-Merciful (Allah) against you, if you are God-fearing.”
t.85: She said, ‘I seek the Lord of Mercy’s protection against you: if you have any fear of Him [do not approach]!’
t.95: Mary exclaimed: "I surely take refuge from you with the Most Compassionate Lord, if you are at all God-fearing."
t.19: She said: Lo! I seek refuge in the Beneficent One from thee, if thou art Allah-fearing.
t.22: She said: "I seek refuge from thee to (Allah) Most Gracious: (come not near) if thou dost fear Allah."
t.203: She said: "Verily! I seek refuge with the Most Gracious (Allâh) from you, if you do fear Allâh."
t.54: یہ کہنے لگیں میں تجھ سے رحمٰن کی پناه مانگتی ہوں اگر تو کچھ بھی اللہ سے ڈرنے واﻻ ہے.

t.149: He said, “I am only a messenger of your Lord to grant you a pure boy.”
t.84: He said, “I am but a message-bearer of your Lord (sent) to give you a boy, purified.”
t.85: but he said, ‘I am but a Mes-senger from your Lord, [come] to announce to you the gift of a pure son.’
t.95: He said: "I am just a message-bearer of your Lord, I have come to grant you a most pure boy."
t.19: He said: I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a faultless son.
t.22: He said: "Nay, I am only a messenger from thy Lord, (to announce) to thee the gift of a holy son.
t.203: (The angel) said: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, (to announce) to you the gift of a righteous son."
t.54: اس نے جواب دیا کہ میں تو اللہ کا بھیجا ہوا قاصد ہوں، تجھے ایک پاکیزه لڑکا دینے آیا ہوں.

t.149: She said, “How can I have a boy when no human being has touched me, nor have I ever been a harlot?”
t.84: She said, “How shall I have a boy while no human has ever touched me, nor have I ever been unchaste?”
t.85: She said, ‘How can I have a son when no man has touched me? I have not been unchaste,’
t.95: Mary said: "How can a boy be born to me when no man has even touched me, nor have I ever been unchaste?"
t.19: She said: How can I have a son when no mortal hath touched me, neither have I been unchaste?
t.22: She said: "How shall I have a son, seeing that no man has touched me, and I am not unchaste?"
t.203: She said: "How can I have a son, when no man has touched me, nor am I unchaste?"
t.54: کہنے لگیں بھلا میرے ہاں بچہ کیسے ہو سکتا ہے؟ مجھے تو کسی انسان کا ہاتھ تک نہیں لگا اور نہ میں بدکار ہوں.

t.149: He said, “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us, and it has been a matter already decreed.’”
t.84: He said, “So it is; your Lord said, ‘It is easy for Me, and (We will do this) so that We make it a sign for people and a mercy from Us, and this is a matter already destined.’”
t.85: and he said, ‘This is what your Lord said: “It is easy for Me- We shall make him a sign to all people, a blessing from Us.”’
t.95: The angel said: "Thus shall it be. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me; and We shall do so in order to make him a Sign for mankind and a mercy from Us. This has been decreed.' "
t.19: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me. And (it will be) that We may make of him a revelation for mankind and a mercy from Us, and it is a thing ordained.
t.22: He said: "So (it will be): Thy Lord saith, 'that is easy for Me: and (We wish) to appoint him as a Sign unto men and a Mercy from Us': It is a matter (so) decreed."
t.203: He said: "So (it will be), your Lord said: ‘That is easy for Me (Allâh): And (We wish) to appoint him as a sign to mankind and a mercy from Us (Allâh), and it is a matter (already) decreed, (by Allâh).’ "
t.54: اس نے کہا بات تو یہی ہے۔ لیکن تیرے پروردگار کا ارشاد ہے کہ وه مجھ پر بہت ہی آسان ہے ہم تو اسے لوگوں کے لئے ایک نشانی بنا دیں گے اور اپنی خاص رحمت، یہ تو ایک طے شده بات ہے.

t.149: So she carried him and secluded herself with him in a remote place.
t.84: So she conceived him, and went in seclusion with him to a remote place.
t.85: And so it was ordained: she conceived him. She withdrew to a distant place
t.95: Then she conceived him and withdrew with him to a far-off place.
t.19: And she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place.
t.22: So she conceived him, and she retired with him to a remote place.
t.203: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place (i.e. Bethlehem valley about 4-6 miles from Jerusalem).
t.54: پس وه حمل سے ہو گئیں اوراسی وجہ سے وه یکسو ہو کر ایک دور کی جگہ چلی گئیں.

t.149: Then the birth pangs compelled her to come to the trunk of the palm tree. She said, “If only I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, completely forgotten!”
t.84: Then the labour pains brought her to the trunk of a palm-tree. She said “O that I would have died before this, and would have been something gone, forgotten.”
t.85: and, when the pains of childbirth drove her to [cling to] the trunk of a palm tree, she exclaimed, ‘I wish I had been dead and forgotten long before all this!’
t.95: Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm-tree and she said: "Oh, would that I had died before this and had been all forgotten."
t.19: And the pangs of childbirth drove her unto the trunk of the palm-tree. She said: Oh, would that I had died ere this and had become a thing of naught, forgotten!
t.22: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm-tree: She cried (in her anguish): "Ah! would that I had died before this! would that I had been a thing forgotten and out of sight!"
t.203: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a date-palm. She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had been forgotten and out of sight!"
t.54: پھر درِد زه ایک کھجور کے تنے کے نیچے لے آیا، بولی کاش! میں اس سے پہلے ہی مر گئی ہوتی اور لوگوں کی یاد سے بھی بھولی بسری ہو جاتی.

t.149: So he called her from beneath her : “Be not sad; your Lord has made a stream beneath you.
t.84: Then he called her from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has placed a stream beneath you.
t.85: but a voice cried to her from below, ‘Do not worry: your Lord has provided a stream at your feet
t.95: Thereupon the angel below her cried out: "Grieve not, for your Lord has caused a stream of water to flow beneath you.
t.19: Then (one) cried unto her from below her, saying: Grieve not! Thy Lord hath placed a rivulet beneath thee,
t.22: But (a voice) cried to her from beneath the (palm-tree): "Grieve not! for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee;
t.203: Then [the babe ‘Îsâ (Jesus) or Jibrîl (Gabriel)] cried unto her from below her, saying: "Grieve not: your Lord has provided a water stream under you.
t.54: اتنے میں اسے نیچے سے ہی آواز دی کہ آزرده خاطر نہ ہو، تیرے رب نے تیرے پاؤں تلے ایک چشمہ جاری کر دیا ہے.

t.149: And shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you—it will drop ripe datesupon you.”
t.84: Shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards yourself and, it will drop upon you ripe fresh dates.
t.85: and, if you shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you, it will deliver fresh ripe dates for you,
t.95: Shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards yourself and fresh and ripe dates shall fall upon you.
t.19: And shake the trunk of the palm-tree toward thee, thou wilt cause ripe dates to fall upon thee.
t.22: "And shake towards thyself the trunk of the palm-tree: It will let fall fresh ripe dates upon thee.
t.203: "And shake the trunk of date-palm towards you, it will let fall fresh ripe-dates upon you."
t.54: اور اس کھجور کے تنے کو اپنی طرف ہلا، یہ تیرے سامنے تروتازه پکی کھجوریں گرا دے گا.

t.149: “So eat and drink and let your eye be comforted, but if you see any human being, say, ‘I have vowed a fast to the All-Merciful, so I will not speak to any human today.’”
t.84: So eat, drink and cool your eyes. Then if you see any human being, say (to him), “I have vowed a fast (of silence) for the All-Merciful (Allah,) and therefore, I shall never speak to any human today.”
t.85: so eat, drink, be glad, and say to anyone you may see: “I have vowed to the Lord of Mercy to abstain from conversation, and I will not talk to anyone today.”’
t.95: So eat and drink and cool your eyes; and if you see any person say to him: 'Verily I have vowed a fast to the Most Compassionate Lord, and so I shall not speak to anyone today.' "
t.19: So eat and drink and be consoled. And if thou meetest any mortal, say: Lo! I have vowed a fast unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal.
t.22: "So eat and drink and cool (thine) eye. And if thou dost see any man, say, 'I have vowed a fast to (Allah) Most Gracious, and this day will I enter into not talk with any human being'"
t.203: "So eat and drink and be glad. And if you see any human being, say: ‘Verily! I have vowed a fast unto the Most Gracious (Allâh) so I shall not speak to any human being this day.’"
t.54: اب چین سے کھا پی اور آنکھیں ٹھنڈی رکھ، اگر تجھے کوئی انسان نظر پڑ جائے تو کہہ دینا کہ میں نے اللہ رحمنٰ کے نام کا روزه مان رکھا ہے۔ میں آج کسی شخص سے بات نہ کروں گی.

t.149: Then she came to her people, carrying him. They said, “O Mary, you have done something terrible.
t.84: Then she came to her people carrying him (the baby). They said, “O Maryam you have committed something grave indeed.
t.85: She went back to her people carrying the child, and they said, ‘Mary! You have done something terrible!
t.95: Then she came to her people, carrying her baby. They said: "O Mary! You have committed a monstrous thing.
t.19: Then she brought him to her own folk, carrying him. They said: O Mary! Thou hast come with an amazing thing.
t.22: At length she brought the (babe) to her people, carrying him (in her arms). They said: "O Mary! truly an amazing thing hast thou brought!
t.203: Then she brought him (the baby) to her people, carrying him. They said: "O Mary! Indeed you have brought a thing Fariyy (a mighty thing). [Tafsir Al-Tabari]
t.54: اب حضرت عیسیٰ (علیہ السلام) کو لئے ہوئے وه اپنی قوم کے پاس آئیں۔ سب کہنے لگے مریم تو نے بڑی بری حرکت کی.

t.149: O sister of Aaron, neither was your father an evil man, nor was your mother a harlot.”
t.84: O sister of Hārūn, neither your father was a man of evil nor was your mother unchaste.”
t.85: Sister of Aaron! Your father was not an evil man; your mother was not unchaste!’
t.95: O sister of Aaron! Your father was not an evil man, nor was your mother an unchaste woman."
t.19: O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a wicked man nor was thy mother a harlot.
t.22: "O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a man of evil, nor thy mother a woman unchaste!"
t.203: "O sister (i.e. the like) of Hârûn (Aaron)! Your father was not a man who used to commit adultery, nor your mother was an unchaste woman."
t.54: اے ہارون کی بہن! نہ تو تیرا باپ برا آدمی تھا اور نہ تیری ماں بدکار تھی.

t.149: So she pointed to him. They said, “How can we speak to an infant in the cradle?”
t.84: So, she pointed towards him (the baby). They said, “How shall we speak to someone who is still a child in the cradle?”
t.85: She pointed at him. They said, ‘How can we converse with an infant?’
t.95: Thereupon Mary pointed to the child. They exclaimed: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a mere child?"
t.19: Then she pointed to him. They said: How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?
t.22: But she pointed to the babe. They said: "How can we talk to one who is a child in the cradle?"
t.203: Then she pointed to him. They said: "How can we talk to one who is a child in the cradle?"
t.54: مریم نے اپنے بچے کی طرف اشاره کیا۔ سب کہنے لگے کہ لو بھلا ہم گود کے بچے سے باتیں کیسے کریں؟

t.149: He said, “I am Allah’s servant. He has brought me the Scripture and has made me a prophet.
t.84: Spoke he (the baby), “Verily I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book, and made me a prophet,
t.85: [But] he said: ‘I am a servant of God. He has granted me the Scripture; made me a prophet;
t.95: The child cried out: "Verily I am Allah's servant. He has granted me the Book and has made me a Prophet
t.19: He spake: Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet,
t.22: He said: "I am indeed a servant of Allah: He hath given me revelation and made me a prophet;
t.203: "He [‘Îsâ (Jesus)] said: "Verily I am a slave of Allâh, He has given me the Scripture and made me a Prophet;"
t.54: بچہ بول اٹھا کہ میں اللہ تعالیٰ کا بنده ہوں۔ اس نے مجھے کتاب عطا فرمائی اور مجھے اپنا پیغمبر بنایا ہے.

t.149: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be and has enjoined upon me prayer and purifying charityso long as I live.
t.84: and He has made me a blessed one wherever I be, and has enjoined Salāh and Zakāh upon me as long as I am alive,
t.85: made me blessed wherever I may be. He commanded me to pray, to give alms as long as I live,
t.95: and has blessed me wherever I might be and has enjoined upon me Prayer and Zakah (purifying alms) as long as I live;
t.19: And hath made me blessed wheresoever I may be, and hath enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving so long as I remain alive,
t.22: "And He hath made me blessed wheresoever I be, and hath enjoined on me Prayer and Charity as long as I live;
t.203: "And He has made me blessed wheresoever I be, and has enjoined on me Salât (prayer), and Zakât, as long as I live."
t.54: اور اس نے مجھے بابرکت کیا ہے جہاں بھی میں ہوں، اور اس نے مجھے نماز اور زکوٰة کا حکم دیا ہے جب تک بھی میں زنده رہوں.

t.149: And He has made me very kind to my mother and has not made me a wretched coercer.
t.84: and (He has made me) good to my mother, and he did not make me oppressive (or) ill-fated.
t.85: to cherish my mother. He did not make me domineering or graceless.
t.95: and has made me dutiful to my mother. He has not made me oppressive, nor bereft of God's blessings.
t.19: And (hath made me) dutiful toward her who bore me, and hath not made me arrogant, unblest.
t.22: "(He) hath made me kind to my mother, and not overbearing or miserable;
t.203: "And dutiful to my mother, and made me not arrogant, unblest.
t.54: اور اس نے مجھے اپنی والده کا خدمت گزار بنایا ہے اور مجھے سرکش اور بدبخت نہیں کیا.

t.149: And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I get resurrected alive.”
t.84: And peace is upon me the day I was born, the day I shall die, and the day I shall be raised alive again.”
t.85: Peace was on me the day I was born, and will be on me the day I die and the day I am raised to life again.’
t.95: Peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I will die, and the day I will be raised up alive."
t.19: Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!
t.22: "So peace is on me the day I was born, the day that I die, and the day that I shall be raised up to life (again)"!
t.203: "And Salâm (peace) be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!"
t.54: اور مجھ پر میری پیدائش کے دن اور میری موت کے دن اور جس دن کہ میں دوباره زنده کھڑا کیا جاؤں گا، سلام ہی سلام ہے.

t.149: That is Jesus, son of Mary—the word of truth about which they are skeptical.
t.84: That is ‘Īsā, the son of Maryam, to say the truth in which they (Christians) are disputing.
t.85: Such was Jesus, son of Mary. [This is] a statement of the Truth about which they are in doubt:
t.95: This is Jesus, the son of Mary; and this is the truth about him concerning which they are in doubt.
t.19: Such was Jesus, son of Mary: (this is) a statement of the truth concerning which they doubt.
t.22: Such (was) Jesus the son of Mary: (it is) a statement of truth, about which they (vainly) dispute.
t.203: Such is ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary). (It is) a statement of truth, about which they doubt (or dispute).
t.54: یہ ہے صحیح واقعہ عیسیٰ بن مریم (علیہ السلام) کا، یہی ہے وه حق بات جس میں لوگ شک وشبہ میں مبتلا ہیں.

t.149: Never was it for Allah to have any offspring—Highly Exalted is He; whenever He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and so it is.
t.84: It is not for Allah to have a son. Pure is He. When He decides a thing, He simply says to it, “Be” and it comes to be.
t.85: it would not befit God to have a child. He is far above that: when He decrees something, He says only, ‘Be,’ and it is.
t.95: It does not befit Allah to take for Himself a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a thing He only says: "Be" and it is.
t.19: It befitteth not (the Majesty of) Allah that He should take unto Himself a son. Glory be to Him! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is.
t.22: It is not befitting to (the majesty of) Allah that He should beget a son. Glory be to Him! when He determines a matter, He only says to it, "Be", and it is.
t.203: It befits not (the Majesty of) Allâh that He should beget a son [this refers to the slander of Christians against Allâh, by saying that ‘Îsâ (Jesus) is the son of Allâh]. Glorified (and Exalted) be He (above all that they associate with Him). When He decrees a thing, He only says to it: "Be!" - and it is.
t.54: اللہ تعالیٰ کے لئے اوﻻد کا ہونا ﻻئق نہیں، وه تو بالکل پاک ذات ہے، وه تو جب کسی کام کے سر انجام دینے کا اراده کرتا ہے تو اسے کہہ دیتا ہے کہ ہو جا، وه اسی وقت ہو جاتا ہے.

t.149: “And indeed, Allah is my Lord and yourLord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.”
t.84: And (O Prophet, say to the people,) “Allah is surely my Lord and your Lord. So, worship Him. This is the straight path.”
t.85: ‘God is my Lord and your Lord, so serve Him: that is a straight path.’
t.95: (Jesus had said): "Indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so serve Him alone. This is the Straight Way."
t.19: And lo! Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So serve Him. That is the right path.
t.22: Verily Allah is my Lord and your Lord: Him therefore serve ye: this is a Way that is straight.
t.203: [‘Îsâ (Jesus) said]: "And verily Allâh is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him (Alone). That is the Straight Path. (Allâh’s religion of Islâmic Monotheism which He did ordain for all of His Prophets)." [Tafsir At-Tabarî]
t.54: میرا اور تم سب کا پروردگار صرف اللہ تعالیٰ ہی ہے۔ تم سب اسی کی عبادت کرو، یہی سیدھی راه ہے.

t.149: But the parties differed among themselves, so woe to those who have denied from the spectacle of a great day.
t.84: Then the groups among them fell in dispute. So, how evil is the fate of the disbelievers when they have to face the Great Day.
t.85: But factions have differed among themselves. What suffering will come to those who obscure the truth when a dreadful Day arrives!
t.95: But different parties began to dispute with one another. A dreadful woe awaits on that great Day for those that reject the Truth.
t.19: The sects among them differ: but woe unto the disbelievers from the meeting of an awful Day.
t.22: But the sects differ among themselves: and woe to the unbelievers because of the (coming) Judgment of a Momentous Day!
t.203: Then the sects differed [i.e. the Christians about ‘Îsâ (Jesus) عليه السلام], so woe unto the disbelievers [those who gave false witness by saying that ‘Îsâ (Jesus) is the son of Allâh] from the Meeting of a great Day (i.e. the Day of Resurrection, when they will be thrown in the blazing Fire).
t.54: پھر یہ فرقے آپس میں اختلاف کرنے لگے، پس کافروں کے لئے ویل ہے ایک بڑے (سخت) دن کی حاضری سے.

t.149: How well they shall hear and see on the day they come to Us! But the unjust are today in evident misguidance.
t.84: How strong will their hearing be, and how strong their vision, the day they will come to Us! But today the transgressors are straying in clear error.
t.85: How sharp of hearing, how sharp of sight they will be when they come to Us, although now they are clearly off course! Warn them [Muhammad] of the Day of Remorse when the matter will be decided,
t.95: How well shall they hear and how well shall they see on the Day they come to Us! But today the evil-doers are in manifest error.
t.19: See and hear them on the Day they come unto Us! yet the evil-doers are to-day in error manifest.
t.22: How plainly will they see and hear, the Day that they will appear before Us! but the unjust today are in error manifest!
t.203: How clearly will they (polytheists and disbelievers in the Oneness of Allâh) see and hear the Day when they will appear before Us! But the Zalimûn (polytheists and wrong-doers) today are in plain error.
t.54: کیا خوب دیکھنے سننے والے ہوں گے اس دن جبکہ ہمارے سامنے حاضر ہوں گے، لیکن آج تو یہ ﻇالم لوگ صریح گمراہی میں پڑے ہوئے ہیں.

t.149: And warnthem of the Day of Regret, when the matter has been concluded. Yet they are in oblivion, and they do not believe.
t.84: Warn them of The Day of Remorse when the whole thing will be settled, while they are heedless and do not believe.
t.85: for they are heedless and do not believe.
t.95: (O Muhammad), warn those who are steeped in heedlessness and are obstinately rejecting the truth that the Day shall come when things will be finally decided and they shall be left with utter remorse.
t.19: And warn them of the Day of anguish when the case hath been decided. Now they are in a state of carelessness, and they believe not.
t.22: But warn them of the Day of Distress, when the matter will be determined: for (behold,) they are negligent and they do not believe!
t.203: And warn them (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) of the Day of grief and regrets, when the case has been decided, while (now) they are in a state of carelessness, and they believe not.
t.54: تو انہیں اس رنج وافسوس کے دن کا ڈر سنا دے جبکہ کام انجام کو پہنچا دیا جائے گا، اور یہ لوگ غفلت اور بے ایمانی میں ہی ره جائیں گے.

t.149: Indeed, We—We alone—will inherit the earth and everyone on it, and to Us they are returned .
t.84: Surely We, only We, shall be the ultimate owner of the earth and all those on it, and to Us they will be returned.
t.85: It is We who will inherit the earth and all who are on it: they will all be returned to Us.
t.95: Ultimately, We shall inherit the earth and whatever is on it; to Us shall they be returned.
t.19: Lo! We, only We, inherit the earth and all who are thereon, and unto Us they are returned.
t.22: It is We Who will inherit the earth, and all beings thereon: to Us will they all be returned.
t.203: Verily We will inherit the earth and whatsoever is thereon. And to Us they all shall be returned,
t.54: خود زمین کے اور تمام زمین والوں کے وارث ہم ہی ہوں گے اور سب لوگ ہماری ہی طرف لوٹا کر ﻻئے جائیں گے.

t.149: And mentionin the Scripture Abraham; he was indeed an unwavering believer(and) a prophet.
t.84: And mention in the Book (the story of) Ibrāhīm. Indeed, he was Siddīq (a man of truth), a prophet,
t.85: Mention too, in the Quran, the story of Abraham. He was a man of truth, a prophet.
t.95: (O Muhammad), recite in the Book the account of Abraham. Most surely he was a man of truth, a Prophet.
t.19: And make mention (O Muhammad) in the Scripture of Abraham. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet.
t.22: (Also mention in the Book (the story of) Abraham: He was a man of Truth, a prophet.
t.203: And mention in the Book (the Qur’ân) Ibrâhîm (Abraham). Verily he was a man of truth, a Prophet.
t.54: اس کتاب میں ابراہیم (علیہ السلام) کا قصہ بیان کر، بیشک وه بڑی سچائی والے پیغمبر تھے.

t.149: Recall when he said to his father, “O my father, why do you worship what can neither hear nor see nor avail you anything?
t.84: when he said to his father, “My dear father, why do you worship something that does neither hear nor see, nor help you in any way?
t.85: He said to his father, ‘Father, why do you worship something that can neither hear nor see nor benefit you in any way?
t.95: (And remind people) when he said to his father: "Father! Why do you worship that which neither sees nor hears, and which can be of no avail to you?
t.19: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee?
t.22: Behold, he said to his father: "O my father! why worship that which heareth not and seeth not, and can profit thee nothing?
t.203: When he said to his father: "O my father! Why do you worship that which hears not, sees not and cannot avail you in anything?
t.54: جبکہ انہوں نے اپنے باپ سے کہا کہ ابّا جان! آپ ان کی پوجا پاٹ کیوں کر رہے ہیں جو نہ سنیں نہ دیکھیں؟ نہ آپ کو کچھ بھی فائده پہنچا سکیں.

t.149: O my father, most surely there has come to me of knowledge what has never come to you, so follow me and I will guide you to a straight path.
t.84: My dear father, indeed there has come to me a knowledge that has not come to you; so, follow me, and I shall lead you to a straight path.
t.85: Father, knowledge that has not reached you has come to me, so follow me: I will guide you to an even path.
t.95: Father, a knowledge that has not reached you has come to me. So follow me that I may guide you to a Straight Way.
t.19: O my father! Lo! there hath come unto me of knowledge that which came not unto thee. So follow me, and I will lead thee on a right path.
t.22: "O my father! to me hath come knowledge which hath not reached thee: so follow me: I will guide thee to a way that is even and straight.
t.203: "O my father! Verily there has come to me of the knowledge that which came not unto you. So follow me, I will guide you to the Straight Path.
t.54: میرے مہربان باپ! آپ دیکھیئے میرے پاس وه علم آیا ہے جو آپ کے پاس آیا ہی نہیں، تو آپ میری ہی مانیں میں بالکل سیدھی راه کی طرف آپ کی رہبری کروں گا.

t.149: O my father, do not worship Satan; indeed Satan has always been disobedient to the All-Merciful.
t.84: My dear father, do not worship the Satan. The Satan is surely rebellious to the All-Merciful, (Allah).
t.85: Father, do not worship Satan- Satan has rebelled against the Lord of Mercy.
t.95: Father, do not serve Satan, for Satan has indeed been a persistent rebel against the Most Compassionate Lord.
t.19: O my father! Serve not the devil. Lo! the devil is a rebel unto the Beneficent.
t.22: "O my father! serve not Satan: for Satan is a rebel against (Allah) Most Gracious.
t.203: "O my father! Worship not Shaitân (Satan). Verily Shaitân (Satan) has been a rebel against the Most Gracious (Allâh).
t.54: میرے ابّا جان آپ شیطان کی پرستش سے باز آجائیں شیطان تو رحم وکرم والے اللہ تعالیٰ کا بڑا ہی نافرمان ہے.

t.149: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the All-Merciful may touch you so that you would become an ally for Satan.”
t.84: My dear father, I fear lest a punishment from the All- Merciful (Allah) should afflict you, and you become a companion of Satan.”
t.85: Father, I fear that a punishment from the Lord of Mercy may afflict you and that you may become Satan’s companion [in Hell].’
t.95: Father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Compassionate Lord might strike you and you may end up as one of Satan's companions?"
t.19: O my father! Lo! I fear lest a punishment from the Beneficent overtake thee so that thou become a comrade of the devil.
t.22: "O my father! I fear lest a Penalty afflict thee from (Allah) Most Gracious, so that thou become to Satan a friend."
t.203: "O my father! Verily I fear lest a torment from the Most Gracious (Allâh) should overtake you, so that you become a companion of Shaitân (Satan) (in the Hell-fire)." [Tafsir Al-Qurtubî]
t.54: ابّا جان! مجھے خوف لگا ہوا کہ کہیں آپ پر کوئی عذاب الٰہی نہ آپڑے کہ آپ شیطان کے ساتھی بن جائیں.

t.149: He said, “Are you renouncing my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you, so leave me for a long while.”
t.84: He said, “Are you averse to my gods O Ibrāhīm? Should you not stop, I will definitely stone you. And leave me for good.”
t.85: His father answered, ‘Abraham, do you reject my gods? I will stone you if you do not stop this. Keep out of my way!’
t.95: The father said: "Abraham, have you turned away from my gods? If you do not give this up, I shall stone you to death. Now begone from me forever."
t.19: He said: Rejectest thou my gods, O Abraham? If thou cease not, I shall surely stone thee. Depart from me a long while!
t.22: (The father) replied: "Dost thou hate my gods, O Abraham? If thou forbear not, I will indeed stone thee: Now get away from me for a good long while!"
t.203: He (the father) said: "Do you reject my gods, O Ibrâhîm (Abraham)? If you stop not (this), I will indeed stone you. So get away from me safely (before I punish you)."
t.54: اس نے جواب دیا کہ اے ابراہیم! کیا تو ہمارے معبودوں سے روگردانی کر رہا ہے۔ سن اگر تو باز نہ آیا تو میں تجھے پتھروں سے مار ڈالوں گا، جا ایک مدت دراز تک مجھ سے الگ ره.

t.149: He said, “Peace be upon you; I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed, He has always been gracious to me.
t.84: He said, “Peace on you. I shall seek forgiveness for you from my Lord. He has always been gracious to me.
t.85: Abraham said, ‘Peace be with you: I will beg my Lord to forgive you- He is always gracious to me-
t.95: Abraham answered: "Peace be upon you. I shall seek pardon for you from my Lord. My Lord has always been kind to Me.
t.19: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me.
t.22: Abraham said: "Peace be on thee: I will pray to my Lord for thy forgiveness: for He is to me Most Gracious.
t.203: Ibrâhîm (Abraham) said: "Peace be on you! I will ask Forgiveness of my Lord for you. Verily He is unto me Ever Most Gracious.
