t.85: He said, ‘What about former generations?’
t.95: Pharaoh asked: "Then, what is the state of the former generations?"
t.19: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old?
t.22: (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the condition of previous generations?"
t.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "What about the generations of old?"
t.54: اس نے کہا اچھا یہ تو بتاؤ اگلے زمانے والوں کا حال کیا ہونا ہے.

t.149: He said, “Knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record; my Lord never goes astray nor does He forget.”
t.84: He replied, “The knowledge about those is with my Lord in a Book. My Lord does neither err nor forget.”
t.85: Moses said, ‘My Lord alone has knowledge of them, all in a record; my Lord does not err or forget.’
t.95: Moses said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord, recorded in the Book. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget."
t.19: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth,
t.22: He replied: "The knowledge of that is with my Lord, duly recorded: my Lord never errs, nor forgets,-
t.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor He forgets."
t.54: جواب دیا کہ ان کا علم میرے رب کے ہاں کتاب میں موجود ہے، نہ تو میرا رب غلطی کرتا ہے نہ بھولتا ہے.

t.149: (He is) the One Who has made the earth a cradle for youand traced in it ways for you, and sent down from the sky water with which Webrought out pairs of diverse plants.

t.85: It was He who spread out the earth for you and traced routes in it. He sent down water from the sky. With that water We bring forth every kind of plant,
t.95: He it is Who spread the earth for you; and made in it paths for you, and sent down water from the sky, and then through it We brought forth many species of diverse plants.
t.19: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation,
t.22: "He Who has, made for you the earth like a carpet spread out; has enabled you to go about therein by roads (and channels); and has sent down water from the sky." With it have We produced diverse pairs of plants each separate from the others.
t.203: Who has made earth for you like a bed (spread out); and has opened roads (ways and paths) for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation.
t.54: اسی نے تمہارے لئے زمین کو فرش بنایا ہے اور اس میں تمہارے چلنے کے لئے راستے بنائے ہیں اور آسمان سے پانی بھی وہی برساتا ہے، پھر اس برسات کی وجہ سے مختلف قسم کی پیداوار بھی ہم ہی پیدا کرتے ہیں.

t.149: Eatand pasture your livestock. Most surely, in that are signs for ones endowed with intelligence.
t.84: Eat, and graze your cattle. Surely, in that there are signs for the people of understanding.
t.85: so eat, and graze your cattle. There are truly signs in all this for people of understand-ing.
t.95: So eat yourself and pasture your cattle. Surely there are many Signs in this for people of understanding.
t.19: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought.
t.22: Eat (for yourselves) and pasture your cattle: verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
t.203: Eat and pasture your cattle (therein); verily, in this are Ayât (proofs and signs) for men of understanding.
t.54: تم خود کھاؤ اور اپنے چوپایوں کو بھی چراؤ۔ کچھ شک نہیں کہ اس میں عقلمندوں کے لئے بہت سی نشانیاں ہیں.

t.84: From this (dust) We created you, and in this we shall put you back, and from this We shall raise you up once again.
t.85: From the earth We created you, into it We shall return you, and from it We shall raise you a second time.
t.95: From this very earth We created you and to the same earth We shall cause you to return, and from it We shall bring you forth to life again.
t.19: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.
t.22: From the (earth) did We create you, and into it shall We return you, and from it shall We bring you out once again.
t.203: Thereof (the earth) We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again.
t.54: اسی زمین میں سے ہم نے تمہیں پیدا کیا اور اسی میں پھر واپس لوٹائیں گے اور اسی سے پھر دوباره تم سب کو نکال کھڑا کریں گے.

t.149: And very truly We showed him all of Our signs, but he disbelieved and refused.
t.84: And We showed him (Pharaoh) all Our signs, yet he rejected and refused.
t.85: We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he denied them and refused [to change].
t.95: Indeed We showed Pharaoh Our Signs, all of them, but he declared them to be false and rejected them.
t.19: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused.
t.22: And We showed Pharaoh all Our Signs, but he did reject and refuse.
t.203: And indeed We showed him [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] all Our Ayât (signs and evidence), but he denied and refused.
t.54: ہم نے اسےاپنی سب نشانیاں دکھا دیں لیکن پھر بھی اس نے جھٹلایا اور انکار کر دیا.

t.149: He said, “Have you come to us to evict us from our land with your sorcery, O Moses?
t.84: Said he, “Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your sorcery, O Mūsā?
t.85: He said, ‘Have you come to drive us from our land with your sorcery, Moses?
t.95: He said: "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land by your sorcery?
t.19: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses?
t.22: He said: "Hast thou come to drive us out of our land with thy magic, O Moses?
t.203: He [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Mûsâ (Moses)?
t.54: کہنے لگا اے موسیٰ! کیا تو اسی لئے آیا ہے کہ ہمیں اپنے جادو کے زور سے ہمارے ملک سے باہر نکال دے.

t.149: We will most surely bring you sorcery like it; so make between us and you an appointment which we will not break—neither us nor you—in a suitable place.”
t.84: We will, then, bring to you a similar sorcery. So, make an appointment between you and us for an even place, not to be backed out, neither by us nor by you.”
t.85: We will confront you with sorcery to match your own: make an appointment between us which neither of us will fail to keep, in a mutually agreeable place.’
t.95: We shall confront you with a sorcery like your own. So appoint a day when both of us might meet face to face in an open space; an appointment which neither we nor you shall fail to keep."
t.19: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both).
t.22: "But we can surely produce magic to match thine! So make a tryst between us and thee, which we shall not fail to keep - neither we nor thou - in a place where both shall have even chances."
t.203: "Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (and beholders could witness the competition)."
t.54: اچھا ہم بھی تیرے مقابلے میں اسی جیسا جادو ضرور ﻻئیں گے پس تو ہمارے اور اپنے درمیان ایک وعدے کا وقت مقرر کر لے، کہ نہ ہم اس کا خلاف کریں اور نہ تو، صاف میدان میں مقابلہ ہو.

t.149: He said, “Yourappointment is the day of the festival, so let the people be herded together at forenoon.”
t.84: He (Mūsā) said, “Your appointment is the festival day, and the people should be assembled at forenoon.”
t.85: He said, ‘Your meeting will be on the day of the feast, so let the people be assembled when the sun has risen high.’
t.95: Moses said: "The appointment to meet you is on the Day of the Feast and let all people come together before noon."
t.19: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high.
t.22: Moses said: "Your tryst is the Day of the Festival, and let the people be assembled when the sun is well up."
t.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon)."
t.54: موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) نے جواب دیا کہ زینت اور جشن کے دن کا وعده ہے اور یہ کہ لوگ دن چڑھے ہی جمع ہو جائیں.

t.149: Then Pharaoh turned away and put together his plot, and then he came.
t.84: So, Pharaoh turned back, and put his plot together, then came.
t.85: Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his resources, then he returned.
t.95: Pharaoh went back and concerted all his stratagem and returned for the encounter.
t.19: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst).
t.22: So Pharaoh withdrew: He concerted his plan, and then came (back).
t.203: So Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) withdrew, devised his plot and then came back.
t.54: پس فرعون لوٹ گیا اور اس نے اپنے ہتھکنڈے جمع کیے پھر آگیا.

t.149: Moses said to them, “Woe to you. Do not fabricate lies against Allah or He will destroy youwith a punishment, and surely, the one who fabricates lies is bound to fail.”
t.84: Mūsā said to them, “Pity on you, do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He should destroy you with a punishment. And loser is he who fabricates a lie.”
t.85: Moses said to them, ‘Beware, do not invent lies against God or He will destroy you with His punishment. Whoever invents lies will fail.’
t.95: (At the time of the encounter) Moses said to them: "Woe to you! Do not invent falsehoods against Allah lest He destroy you with a scourge. Surely those who invent lies shall come to grief."
t.19: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably.
t.22: Moses said to him: Woe to you! Forge not ye a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you (at once) utterly by chastisement: the forger must suffer frustration!"
t.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said to them: "Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allâh, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allâh) will fail miserably."
t.54: موسی (علیہ السلام) نے ان سے کہا تمہاری شامت آچکی، اللہ تعالیٰ پر جھوٹ اور افترا نہ باندھو کہ وه تمہیں عذابوں سے ملیا میٹ کر دے، یاد رکھو وه کبھی کامیاب نہ ہوگا جس نے جھوٹی بات گھڑی.

t.149: Then they disagreed with each other about their matter and conversed secretly.
t.84: Then, they disputed among themselves in their matter, and kept their talk secret.
t.85: So they discussed their plan among themselves, talking secretly,
t.95: Thereupon they wrangled among themselves about the matter and conferred in secret.
t.19: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret.
t.22: So they disputed, one with another, over their affair, but they kept their talk secret.
t.203: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret.
t.54: پس یہ لوگ آپس کے مشوروں میں مختلف رائے ہوگئے اور چھﭗ کر چپکے چپکے مشوره کرنے لگے.

t.149: They said, “These two are nothing but sorcerers who want to evict you from your land with their sorcery and abolish your exemplary way of life.
t.84: Said they, “Certainly, these two are sorcerers who wish to drive you out from your land, and do away with your excellent way of life.
t.85: saying, ‘These two men are sorcerers. Their purpose is to drive you out of your land with their sorcery and put an end to your time-honoured way of life.
t.95: Some of them said: "These two are magicians, who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and to destroy your excellent way of life.
t.19: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions;
t.22: They said: "These two are certainly (expert) magicians: their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to do away with your most cherished institutions.
t.203: They said: "Verily these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with magic, and overcome your chiefs and nobles.
t.54: کہنے لگے یہ دونوں محض جادوگر ہیں اور ان کا پختہ اراده ہے کہ اپنے جادو کے زور سے تمہیں تمہارے ملک سے نکال باہر کر دیں اور تمہارے بہترین مذہب کو برباد کر دیں.

t.149: So decide yourplot, then come, lined up(in ranks) ; and the one who gains the upper hand is surely bound to succeed today.”
t.84: So, make your plot firm and come forth in one row. Successful today is the one who prevails.”
t.85: So gather your resources and line up for the contest. Whoever wins today is sure to prosper.’
t.95: So muster all your stratagem and come forth in a row. Whoever prevails today shall triumph."
t.19: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.
t.22: "Therefore concert your plan, and then assemble in (serried) ranks: He wins (all along) today who gains the upper hand."
t.203: "So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful."
t.54: تو تم بھی اپنا کوئی داؤ اٹھا نہ رکھو، پھر صف بندی کرکے آؤ۔ جو غالب آگیا وہی بازی لے گیا.

t.149: They said, “O Moses, either you cast or we will be the first to cast.”
t.84: They said, “O Mūsā, either you throw (first), or shall we be first to throw?”
t.85: They said, ‘Moses, will you throw first or shall we?’
t.95: The magicians said: "Moses, will you throw down or shall we be the first to throw?"
t.19: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw?
t.22: They said: "O Moses! whether wilt thou that thou throw (first) or that we be the first to throw?"
t.203: They said: "O Mûsâ (Moses)! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?"
t.54: کہنے لگے کہ اے موسیٰ! یا تو تو پہلے ڈال یا ہم پہلے ڈالنے والے بن جائیں.

t.149: He said, “Rather, youcast.” And suddenly, their ropes and staffs were made to appear to him, because of their sorcery, to be slithering.
t.84: He said, “Rather, you throw.” Then, suddenly their ropes and sticks seemed to him, due to their magic, as if they were running.
t.85: ‘You throw,’ said Moses, and––lo and behold!––through their sorcery, their ropes and staffs seemed to him to be moving.
t.95: Moses replied: "No, let it be you to throw first." Then suddenly it appeared to Moses, owing to their magic, as if their ropes and staffs were running.
t.19: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran.
t.22: He said, "Nay, throw ye first!" Then behold their ropes and their rods-so it seemed to him on account of their magic - began to be in lively motion!
t.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Nay, throw you (first)!" Then behold! their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast.
t.54: جواب دیا کہ نہیں تم ہی پہلے ڈالو۔ اب تو موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) کو یہ خیال گزرنے لگا کہ ان کی رسیاں اور لکڑیاں ان کے جادو کے زور سے دوڑ بھاگ رہی ہیں.

t.149: So Moses felt apprehensive within himself.
t.84: So, Mūsā concealed some fear in his heart.
t.85: Moses was inwardly alarmed,
t.95: So Moses' heart was filled with fear.
t.19: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind.
t.22: So Moses conceived in his mind a (sort of) fear.
t.203: So Mûsâ (Moses) conceived fear in himself.
t.54: پس موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) نے اپنے دل ہی دل میں ڈر محسوس کیا.

t.149: We said, “Be not afraid; youare the highest.
t.84: We said, “Do not be scared. Certainly, you are to be the upper most.
t.85: but We said, ‘Do not be afraid, you have the upper hand.
t.95: We said to him: "Have no fear; for it is you who will prevail.
t.19: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher.
t.22: We said: "Fear not! for thou hast indeed the upper hand:
t.203: We (Allâh) said: "Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand.
t.54: ہم نے فرمایا کچھ خوف نہ کر یقیناً تو ہی غالب اور برتر رہے گا.

t.149: And cast what is in your right hand—it will swallow what they have crafted; what they have crafted is only a sorcerer’s trickery, for the sorcerer will not succeed wherever he may go.”
t.84: And throw what is in your right hand, and it will devour what they have concocted. What they have concocted is but a sleight of a magician. And the magician does not succeed wherever he comes from.”
t.85: Throw down what is in your right hand: it will swallow up what they have produced. They have only produced the tricks of a sorcerer, and a sorcerer will not prosper, wherever he goes.’
t.95: And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up all that they have wrought. They have wrought only a magician's stratagem. A magician cannot come to any good, come whence he may."
t.19: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.
t.22: "Throw that which is in thy right hand: Quickly will it swallow up that which they have faked what they have faked is but a magician's trick: and the magician thrives not, (no matter) where he goes."
t.203: "And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician’s trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain."
t.54: اور تیرے دائیں ہاتھ میں جو ہے اسے ڈالدے کہ ان کی تمام کاریگری کووه نگل جائے، انہوں نے جو کچھ بنایا ہے یہ صرف جادوگروں کے کرتب ہیں اور جادوگر کہیں سے بھی آئے کامیاب نہیں ہوتا.

t.149: So the sorcerers fell down prostrate. They said, “We have attained faith in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
t.84: So, the magicians were led (by the truth) to fall in prostration. They said, “We have (now) believed in the Lord of Hārūn and Mūsā.”
t.85: [So it was, and] the sorcerers threw themselves down in submission. ‘We believe,’ they said, ‘in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’
t.95: Eventually the magicians were impelled to fall down prostrate and said: "We believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron."
t.19: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
t.22: So the magicians were thrown down to prostration: they said, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses".
t.203: So the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Hârûn (Aaron) and Mûsâ (Moses)."
t.54: اب تو تمام جادوگر سجدے میں گر پڑے اور پکار اٹھے کہ ہم تو ہارون اور موسیٰ (علیہما السلام) کے رب پر ایمان ﻻئے.

t.149: He said, “Have youattained faith in him before I have given you permission? He must be your chief who has taught you sorcery. So I will most surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides, and I will most surely crucify you on the trunks of the palm-trees. Then you will most surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.”
t.84: He (Pharaoh) said, “You have believed in him before I permit you. This man is in fact your master who has taught you the magic. So I will certainly cut off your hands and your legs from opposite sides, and will crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees, and you shall know whose punishment, out of us, is more severe and more lasting.”
t.85: Pharaoh said, ‘How dare you believe in him before I have given you permission? This must be your master, the man who taught you witchcraft. I shall certainly cut off your alternate hands and feet, then crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. You will know for certain which of us has the fiercer and more lasting punishment.’
t.95: Pharaoh said: "What! Did you believe in Him even before I permitted you to do so? Surely, he must be your chief who taught you magic. Now I will certainly cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and will crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees, and then you will come to know which of us can inflict sterner and more lasting torment."
t.19: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment.
t.22: (Pharaoh) said: "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? Surely this must be your leader, who has taught you magic! be sure I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will have you crucified on trunks of palm-trees: so shall ye know for certain, which of us can give the more severe and the more lasting punishment!"
t.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Believe you in him [Mûsâ (Moses)] before I give you permission? Verily he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms, and you shall surely know which of us [I (Fir‘aun - Pharaoh) or the Lord of Mûsâ (Moses) (Allâh)] can give the severe and more lasting torment."
t.54: فرعون کہنے لگا کہ کیا میری اجازت سے پہلے ہی تم اس پرایمان لے آئے؟ یقیناً یہی تمہارا وه بڑا بزرگ ہے جس نے تم سب کو جادو سکھایا ہے، (سن لو) میں تمہارے پاؤں الٹے سیدھے کٹوا کر تم سب کو کھجور کے تنوں میں سولی پر لٹکوا دوں گا، اور تمہیں پوری طرح معلوم ہوجائے گا کہ ہم میں سے کس کی مار زیاده سخت اور دیرپا ہے.

t.149: They said, “We will not prefer you over what has come to us of evident proofs nor(over) the One Who originated us, so decree whatever you decree; you can only decree for this Earlier Life.
t.84: They said, “We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us, and over Him who has created us. So, decide whatever you have to decide. You will decide only for this worldly life.
t.85: They said, ‘We shall never prefer you to the clear sign that has come to us, nor to Him who created us. So decide whatever you will: you can only decide matters of this present life-
t.95: The magicians answered: "By Him Who has created us, we shall never prefer you to the Truth after manifest Signs have come to us. So decree whatever you will. Your decree will pertain, at the most, to the present life of the world.
t.19: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world.
t.22: They said: "Never shall we regard thee as more than the Clear Signs that have come to us, or than Him Who created us! so decree whatever thou desirest to decree: for thou canst only decree (touching) the life of this world.
t.203: They said: "We prefer you not over what have come to us of the clear signs and to Him (Allâh) Who created us. So decree whatever you desire to decree, for you can only decree (regarding) this life of the world.
t.54: انہوں نے جواب دیا کہ ناممکن ہے کہ ہم تجھے ترجیح دیں ان دلیلوں پر جو ہمارے سامنے آچکیں اور اس اللہ پر جس نے ہمیں پیدا کیا ہے اب تو تو جو کچھ کرنے وﻻ ہے کر گزر، تو جو کچھ بھی حکم چلا سکتا ہے وه اسی دنیوی زندگی میں ہی ہے.

t.149: We have indeed attained faith in our Lord so that He may forgive us our offenses and what you have compelled us to practice of sorcery, for Allah is better and more lasting.”
t.84: We have put our faith in our Lord, so that He forgives us for our sins and for the magic you compelled us to perform. And Allah is the Best and Everlasting.”
t.85: we believe in our Lord, [hoping] He may forgive us our sins and the sorcery that you forced us to practise- God is better and more lasting.’
t.95: We believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and also forgive us the practice of magic to which you had compelled us. Allah is the Best and He alone will abide."
t.19: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting.
t.22: "For us, we have believed in our Lord: may He forgive us our faults, and the magic to which thou didst compel us: for Allah is Best and Most Abiding."
t.203: "Verily we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allâh is better as regards reward in comparison to your [Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh)] reward, and more lasting (as regards punishment in comparison to your punishment)."
t.54: ہم (اس امید سے) اپنے پروردگار پرایمان ﻻئے کہ وه ہماری خطائیں معاف فرما دے اور (خاص کر) جادوگری (کا گناه،) جس پر تم نے ہمیں مجبور کیا ہے، اللہ ہی بہتر اور ہمیشہ باقی رہنے واﻻ ہے.

t.149: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then surely for him is Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
t.84: Surely whoever comes to his Lord as a sinner, for him there is Jahannam in which he neither will die nor will live (a happy life).
t.85: Hell will be the reward of those who return to their Lord as evildoers: there they will stay, neither living nor dying.
t.95: The truth is that Hell awaits him who comes to his Lord laden with sin; he shall neither die in it nor live.
t.19: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live.
t.22: Verily he who comes to his Lord as a sinner (at Judgment),- for him is Hell: therein shall he neither die nor live.
t.203: Verily whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, sinner, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allâh and His Messengers), then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live.
t.54: بات یہی ہے کہ جو بھی گنہگار بن کر اللہ تعالیٰ کے ہاں حاضر ہوگا اس کے لئے دوزخ ہے، جہاں نہ موت ہوگی اور نہ زندگی.

t.149: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds, then for thoseare the highest degrees(of rank) :
t.84: And whoever will come to Him as believer, having done righteous deeds, for such people there are the highest ranks,
t.85: But those who return to their Lord as believers with righteous deeds will be rewarded with the highest of ranks,
t.95: But he who comes to Him with faith and righteous works shall be exalted to high ranks,
t.19: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations;
t.22: But such as come to Him as Believers who have worked righteous deeds,- for them are ranks exalted,-
t.203: But whoever comes to Him (Allâh) as a believer (in the Oneness of Allâh), and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (in the Hereafter), -
t.54: اور جو بھی اس کے پاس ایمان کی حالت میں حاضر ہوگا اور اس نے اعمال بھی نیک کیے ہوں گے اس کے لئے بلند وباﻻ درجے ہیں.

t.149: Gardens of Perpetuity beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, for that is the repayment of the one who purifies himself.
t.84: the eternal gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which they shall live for ever. That is the reward for the one who has purified himself.
t.85: Gardens of lasting bliss graced with flowing streams, and there they will stay. Such is the reward of those who purify themselves.
t.95: and shall live for ever in everlasting Gardens beneath which rivers flow. Such will be the reward of those who purify themselves.
t.19: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.
t.22: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers: they will dwell therein for aye: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (from evil).
t.203: ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (by abstaining from all kinds of sins and evil deeds which Allâh has forbidden and by doing all that Allâh has ordained).
t.54: ہمیشگی والی جنتیں جن کے نیچے نہریں لہریں لے رہی ہیں جہاں وه ہمیشہ (ہمیشہ) رہیں گے۔ یہی انعام ہے ہر اس شخص کا جو پاک ہوا.

t.149: And very truly, We revealed to Moses: “Journey by night with My servants and strike for them a dry road across the sea. You will not be afraidof being overtaken nor apprehensive.”
t.84: And We revealed to Mūsā saying, “Set out with my servants at night, then make for them a dry path across the sea (with the strike of your staff), neither fearing to be caught up, nor having any fear (of drowning).”
t.85: We revealed to Moses, ‘Go out at night with My servants and strike a dry path for them across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken and do not be dismayed.’
t.95: Most certainly We revealed to Moses: "Proceed with My servants in the night and strike for them a dry path in the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be afraid of treading through the sea."
t.19: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea).
t.22: We sent an inspiration to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, and strike a dry path for them through the sea, without fear of being overtaken (by Pharaoh) and without (any other) fear."
t.203: And indeed We revealed to Mûsâ (Moses) (saying): "Travel by night with Ibâdi (My slaves) and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] nor being afraid (of drowning in the sea)."
t.54: ہم نے موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) کی طرف وحی نازل فرمائی کہ تو راتوں رات میرے بندوں کو لے چل، اور ان کے لئے دریا میں خشک راستہ بنا لے، پھر نہ تجھے کسی کے آپکڑنے کا خطره ہوگا نہ ڈر.

t.149: So Pharaoh pursued them with his troops, but there overwhelmed them of the waters that which overwhelmed them.
t.84: Then Pharaoh chased them with his troops. So, they were encircled by that (huge wave) from the sea which overwhelmed them.
t.85: Pharaoh pursued them with his armies and was overwhelmed by the sea.
t.95: Pharaoh pursued them with his hosts, but they were fully overwhelmed by the sea.
t.19: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea.
t.22: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his forces, but the waters completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
t.203: Then Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) pursued them with his hosts, but the sea-water completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
t.54: فرعون نے اپنے لشکروں سمیت ان کا تعاقب کیا پھر تو دریا ان سب پر چھا گیا جیسا کچھ چھا جانے واﻻ تھا.

t.149: Thus Pharaoh led his people astray and never did he guide(them) .
t.84: Pharaoh held his people astray, and did not show them the right path.
t.85: Pharaoh truly led his people astray; he did not guide them.
t.95: Pharaoh led his people astray; he did not guide them aright.
t.19: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them.
t.22: Pharaoh led his people astray instead of leading them aright.
t.203: And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) led his people astray, and he did not guide them.
t.54: فرعون نے اپنی قوم کو گمراہی میں ڈال دیا اور سیدھا راستہ نہ دکھایا.

t.149: O Children of Israel, We have surely saved youfrom your enemy, and have made an appointment with you by the right side of Mount Tûr, and sent down to you manna and quails.
t.84: O children of Isrā’īl , We delivered you from your enemy and appointed for you the right side of the mount Tūr (Sinai), and sent down for you the Mann and Salwā :
t.85: Children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemies. We made a pledge with you on the right-hand side of the mountain. We sent down manna and quails for you,
t.95: Children of Israel! We saved you from your enemy and made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount and sent down on you manna and quails,
t.19: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain's side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails,
t.22: O ye Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a Covenant with you on the right side of Mount (Sinai), and We sent down to you Manna and quails:
t.203: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you Al-Manna and quails,
t.54: اے بنی اسرائیل! دیکھو ہم نے تمہیں تمہارے دشمن سے نجات دی اور تم سے کوه طور کی دائیں طرف کا وعده کیا اور تم پر من وسلویٰ اتارا.

t.149: Eat of the good things We have provided for you, but do not exceed the limits in it lest you deserveMy wrath upon you, for the one upon whom My wrath is deserved has surely fallen.
t.84: Eat from the good things We have provided to you, and do not exceed the limits in it, lest My wrath should descend on you. The one upon whom My wrath descends certainly falls into destruction.
t.85: ‘Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not overstep the bounds, or My wrath will descend on you. Anyone on whom My wrath descends has truly fallen.
t.95: saying: "Partake of the good things that We have provided for you, but do not transgress lest My wrath fall upon you; for he upon whom My wrath falls is ruined.
t.19: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed.
t.22: (Saying): "Eat of the good things We have provided for your sustenance, but commit no excess therein, lest My Wrath should justly descend on you: and those on whom descends My Wrath do perish indeed!
t.203: (Saying) eat of the Tayyibât (good lawful things) wherewith We have provided you, and commit no transgression or oppression therein, lest My Anger should justly descend on you. And he on whom My Anger descends, he is indeed perished. [Tafsir At-Tabari]
t.54: تم ہماری دی ہوئی پاکیزه روزی کھاؤ، اور اس میں حد سے آگے نہ بڑھو، ورنہ تم پر میرا غضب نازل ہوگا، اور جس پر میرا غضب نازل ہو جائے وه یقیناً تباه ہوا.

t.149: And very truly I am Forgiving towards the one who repented and attained faith and acted righteously and then remained guided.
t.84: Surely I am the Most-Forgiving for him who repents and believes and acts righteously, then follows the right path.
t.85: Yet I am most forgiving towards those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and stay on the right path.’
t.95: But I am indeed Most Forgiving to him who repents and believes and does righteous works and keeps to the Right Way."
t.19: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.
t.22: "But, without doubt, I am (also) He that forgives again and again, to those who repent, believe, and do right, who,- in fine, are ready to receive true guidance."
t.203: And verily, I am indeed forgiving to him who repents, believes (in My Oneness, and associates none in worship with Me) and does righteous good deeds, and then remains constant in doing them, (till his death).
t.54: ہاں بیشک میں انہیں بخش دینے واﻻ ہوں جو توبہ کریں ایمان ﻻئیں نیک عمل کریں اور راه راست پر بھی رہیں.

t.149: “And what made you rush ahead of your people, O Moses?”
t.84: “What has caused you to hurry before your people, O Mūsā?”
t.85: [God said], ‘Moses, what has made you come ahead of your people in such haste?’
t.95: "But, O Moses, what has made you come in haste from your people?"
t.19: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses?
t.22: (When Moses was up on the Mount, Allah said:) "What made thee hasten in advance of thy people, O Moses?"
t.203: "And what made you hasten from your people, O Mûsâ (Moses)?"
t.54: اے موسیٰ! تجھے اپنی قوم سے (غافل کرکے) کون سی چیز جلدی لے آئی؟

t.149: He said, “They are following in my footsteps. And I hurried on to You, my Lord, that You may be well pleased.”
t.84: He said, “Here they are just behind me, and I hurried towards You, my Lord, so that You be pleased.”
t.85: and he said, ‘They are following in my footsteps. I rushed to You, Lord, to please You,’
t.95: He said: "They are close behind me, and I hastened to You, Lord, that You may be pleased with me."
t.19: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased.
t.22: He replied: "Behold, they are close on my footsteps: I hastened to thee, O my Lord, to please thee."
t.203: He said: "They are close on my footsteps: and I hastened to You, O my Lord, that You might be pleased."
t.54: کہا کہ وه لوگ بھی میرے پیچھے ہی پیچھے ہیں، اور میں نے اے رب! تیری طرف جلدی اس لئے کی کہ تو خوش ہو جائے.

t.149: He said, “Yet, We have surely tested your people in your absence, and the Samiri led them astray.”
t.84: He said, “We have then put your people to test after you (left them) and Sāmiriyy has misguided them.”
t.85: but God said, ‘We have tested your people in your absence: the Samiri has led them astray.’
t.95: Said He: "Verily We tested your people in your absence and the Samiri led them astray."
t.19: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them.
t.22: (Allah) said: "We have tested thy people in thy absence: the Samiri has led them astray."
t.203: (Allâh) said: "Verily We have tried your people in your absence, and As-Sâmirî has led them astray."
t.54: فرمایا! ہم نے تیری قوم کو تیرے پیچھے آزمائش میں ڈال دیا اور انہیں سامری نے بہکا دیا ہے.

t.149: So Moses returned to his people, wrathful(and) sorrowful. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Was the(time of the) covenant too long for you? Or did you want wrath from your Lord to descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?”
t.84: So, Mūsā went back to his people, angry and sad. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Did then the time become too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord befalls you, and hence you broke your promise to me?”
t.85: Moses returned to his people, angry and aggrieved. He said, ‘My people, did your Lord not make you a gracious promise? Was my absence too long for you? Did you want anger to fall on you from your Lord and so broke your word to me?’
t.95: Moses returned to his people full of wrath and grief, and said: "My people! Has your Lord not made good an excellent promise He made to you? And has a long time passed since those promises were fulfilled? Or was it to incur the wrath of your Lord that you broke your promise with me?"
t.19: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me?
t.22: So Moses returned to his people in a state of indignation and sorrow. He said: "O my people! did not your Lord make a handsome promise to you? Did then the promise seem to you long (in coming)? Or did ye desire that Wrath should descend from your Lord on you, and so ye broke your promise to me?"
t.203: Then Mûsâ (Moses) returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow. He said: "O my people! Did not your Lord promise you a fair promise? Did then the promise seem to you long in coming? Or did you desire that wrath should descend from your Lord on you, that you broke your promise to me (i.e disbelieving in Allâh and worshipping the calf)?"
t.54: پس موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) سخت غضبناک ہو کر رنج کے ساتھ واپس لوٹے، اور کہنے لگے کہ اے میری قوم والو! کیا تم سے تمہارے پروردگار نے نیک وعده نہیں کیا تھا؟ کیا اس کی مدت تمہیں لمبی معلوم ہوئی؟ بلکہ تمہارا اراده ہی یہ ہے کہ تم پر تمہارے پروردگار کا غضب نازل ہو؟ کہ تم نے میرے وعدے کا خلاف کیا.

t.149: They said, “We did not break our promise to you by our choice, but we were made to carry burdens of the people’s ornaments, so we cast them and so did the Samiri cast.”
t.84: They said, “We did not break our promise to you of our own accord, but we were burdened with loads from the ornaments of the people;so we threw them, and thus did Sāmiriyy cast.”
t.85: They said, ‘We did not break our word to you deliberately. We were burdened with the weight of people’s jewellery, so we threw it [into the fire], and the Samiri did the same,’
t.95: They answered: "We did not break our promise with you out of our own volition; but we were laden with the load of people's ornaments, and we simply threw them down(into the fire), and the Samiri also threw down something,
t.19: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed.
t.22: They said: "We broke not the promise to thee, as far as lay in our power: but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the (whole) people, and we threw them (into the fire), and that was what the Samiri suggested.
t.203: They said: "We broke not the promise to you, of our own will, but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the [Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh)] people, then we cast them (into the fire), and that was what As-Sâmirî suggested."
t.54: انہوں نے جواب دیا کہ ہم نے اپنےاختیار سے آپ کے ساتھ وعدے کا خلاف نہیں کیا۔ بلکہ ہم پر زیورات قوم کے جو بوجھ ﻻد دیے گئے تھے انہیں ہم نے ڈال دیا، اور اسی طرح سامری نے بھی ڈال دیئے.

t.149: So he brought out for them a calf—a mere body with a lowing sound. And theysaid, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but he has forgotten.”
t.84: Then he brought forth for them a calf, which was (merely) a body with a lowing sound. Then they said, “This is your god and the god of Mūsā, and he (Mūsā) erred.”
t.85: but he [used the molten jewellery to] produce an image of a calf which made a lowing sound, and they said, ‘This is your god and Moses’ god, but he has forgotten.’
t.95: and brought out of there (from the molten gold) the effigy of a calf that lowed." The people cried out: "This is your deity and the deity of Moses, whom Moses has forgotten."
t.19: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.
t.22: "Then he brought out (of the fire) before the (people) the image of a calf: It seemed to low: so they said: This is your god, and the god of Moses, but (Moses) has forgotten!"
t.203: Then he took out (of the fire) for them (a statue of) a calf which seemed to low. They said: "This is your ilâh (god), and the ilâh (god) of Mûsâ (Moses), but he [Mûsâ (Moses)] has forgotten (his god).’"
t.54: پھر اس نے لوگوں کے لئے ایک بچھڑا نکال کھڑا کیا یعنی بچھڑے کا بت، جس کی گائے کی سی آواز بھی تھی پھر کہنے لگے کہ یہی تمہارا معبود ہے اور موسیٰ کا بھی، لیکن موسیٰ بھول گیا ہے.

t.149: Do they not see that it cannot return a word to them, nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?
t.84: Have they not been seeing that it did not respond to them (even) with a word, nor did it have power to harm or benefit them?
t.85: Did they not see that [the calf] gave them no answer, that it had no power to harm or benefit them?
t.95: Did they not see that it did not return a word to them, and had no power either to hurt them or to cause them any benefit?
t.19: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use?
t.22: Could they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
t.203: Did they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
t.54: کیا یہ گمراه لوگ یہ بھی نہیں دیکھتے کہ وه تو ان کی بات کا جواب بھی نہیں دے سکتا اور نہ ان کے کسی برے بھلے کا اختیار رکھتا ہے.

t.149: And Aaron had most surely said to them before, “O my people, you are indeed being tested by this, and indeed your Lord is the All-Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.”
t.84: Hārūn had already said to them, “O my people, you have only been led astray with it, and your Lord is the RaHmān (All-Merciful). So follow me and obey my command.”
t.85: Aaron did say to them, ‘My people, this calf is a test for you. Your true Lord is the Lord of Mercy, so follow me and obey my orders,’
t.95: Certainly Aaron had said to them even before (the return of Moses): "My people, you were fallen into error because of the calf. Surely your Lord is Most Compassionate; so follow me and obey my command."
t.19: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order.
t.22: Aaron had already, before this said to them: "O my people! ye are being tested in this: for verily your Lord is (Allah) Most Gracious; so follow me and obey my command."
t.203: And Hârûn (Aaron) indeed had said to them beforehand: "O my people! You are being tried in this, and verily, your Lord is (Allâh) the Most Gracious, so follow me and obey my order."
t.54: اور ہارون (علیہ السلام) نےاس سے پہلے ہی ان سے کہہ دیا تھا اے میری قوم والو! اس بچھڑے سے تو صرف تمہاری آزمائش کی گئی ہے، تمہارا حقیقی پروردگار تو اللہ رحمنٰ ہی ہے، پس تم سب میری تابعداری کرو۔ اور میری بات مانتے چلے جاؤ.*

t.149: They said, “We will not give up consecrating it until Moses returns to us.”
t.84: They said, “We will never cease to stay with it in devotion, until Mūsā returns to us.”
t.85: but they replied, ‘We shall not give up our devotion to it until Moses returns to us.’
t.95: But they answered: "By no means shall we cease to worship it until Moses returns to us."
t.19: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us.
t.22: They had said: "We will not abandon this cult, but we will devote ourselves to it until Moses returns to us."
t.203: They said: "We will not stop worshipping it (i.e. the calf), until Mûsâ (Moses) returns to us."
t.54: انہوں نے جواب دیا کہ موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) کی واپسی تک تو ہم اسی کے مجاور بنے بیٹھے رہیں گے.

t.149: He said, “O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
t.84: He (Mūsā) said, “O Hārūn, what did prevent you from following me when you saw them going astray?
t.85: Moses said, ‘When you realized they had gone astray, what prevented you, Aaron,
t.95: (After rebuking his people) Moses turned to Aaron and said: "Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
t.19: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray,
t.22: (Moses) said: "O Aaron! what kept thee back, when thou sawest them going wrong,
t.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "O Hârûn (Aaron)! What prevented you when you saw them going astray;
t.54: موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) کہنے لگے اے ہارون! انہیں گمراه ہوتا ہوا دیکھتے ہوئے تجھے کس چیز نے روکا تھا.

t.149: from following me? Have you disobeyed my command?”
t.84: Did you then disobey my command?”
t.85: from coming after me? How could you disobey my orders?’
t.95: from following my way? Have you disobeyed my command?"
t.19: That thou followedst me not? Hast thou then disobeyed my order?
t.22: "From following me? Didst thou then disobey my order?"
t.203: "That you followed me not (according to my advice to you)? Have you then disobeyed my order?"
t.54: کہ تو میرے پیچھے نہ آیا۔ کیا تو بھی میرے فرمان کا نافرمان بن بیٹھا.

t.149: He said, “O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard nor by my head; I feared you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel and have not regarded my word.’”
t.84: He said, “O son of my mother, do not hold me by my beard, nor by my head. I feared that you would say, ‘You have caused discord among the children of Isrā’īl and did not observe my advice.’”
t.85: He said, ‘Son of my mother- let go of my beard and my hair!- I was afraid you would say, “You have caused division among the children of Israel and have not heeded what I said.”’
t.95: Aaron answered: "Son of my mother! Do not seize me with my beard, nor by (the hair of) my head. I feared that on returning you might say: 'You sowed discord among the Children of Israel, and did not pay heed to my words.'"
t.19: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word.
t.22: (Aaron) replied: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard nor by (the hair of) my head! Truly I feared lest thou shouldst say, 'Thou has caused a division among the children of Israel, and thou didst not respect my word!'"
t.203: He [Hârûn (Aaron)] said: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard, nor by my head! Verily, I feared lest you should say: ‘You have caused a division among the Children of Israel, and you have not respected my word!’ "
t.54: ہارون (علیہ السلام) نے کہا اے میرے ماں جائے بھائی! میری داڑھی نہ پکڑ اور سر کے بال نہ کھینچ، مجھے تو صرف یہ خیال دامن گیر ہوا کہ کہیں آپ یہ (نہ) فرمائیں کہ تو نے بنی اسرائیل میں تفرقہ ڈال دیا اور میری بات کا انتظار نہ کیا.

t.149: He said, “What do you have to say, O Samiri?”
t.84: He (Mūsā) said, “What then is your case, O Sāmiriyy?”
t.85: Moses said, ‘And what was the matter with you, Samiri?’
t.95: Moses said: "What, then, is your case, O Samiri?"
t.19: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri?
t.22: (Moses) said: "What then is thy case, O Samiri?"
t.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "And what is the matter with you. O Sâmirî? (i.e. why did you do so?)"
t.54: موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) نے پوچھا سامری تیرا کیا معاملہ ہے.

t.149: He said, “I perceived what they did not perceive, so I grasped a handful from the messenger’s traces and I flung it away, and thus my soul prompted me.”
t.84: He said, “I perceived something they did not perceive. So I picked up a handful from under the footstep of the messenger. Then, I cast it. And thus my inner self tempted me.”
t.85: He replied, ‘I saw something they did not; I took in some of the teachings of the Messenger but tossed them aside: my soul prompted me to do what I did.’
t.95: He answered: "I saw what the people did not see. So I took a handful of dust from the trail of the Messenger, and I flung it (into the fire). Thus did my mind prompt me."
t.19: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me.
t.22: He replied: "I saw what they saw not: so I took a handful (of dust) from the footprint of the Messenger, and threw it (into the calf): thus did my soul suggest to me."
t.203: (Sâmirî) said: "I saw what they saw not, so I took a handful (of dust) from the (hoof) print of the messenger [Jibrîl’s (Gabriel) horse] and threw it [into the fire in which were put the ornaments of Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh) people, or into the calf]. Thus my inner-self suggested to me."
t.54: اس نے جواب دیا کہ مجھے وه چیز دکھائی دی جو انہیں دکھائی نہیں دی، تو میں نے فرستادہٴ الٰہی کے نقش قدم سے ایک مٹھی بھر لی اسے اس میں ڈال دیا اسی طرح میرے دل نے یہ بات میرے لئے بھلی بنا دی.

t.149: He said, “Be gone! For indeed your lot in this life is to say, ‘No touching’, and indeed you have an appointment that you will not be allowed to break . And look at your god that you kept consecrating—we will certainly burn it up then blow it away completely into the waters.”
t.84: He (Mūsā) said, “Then go away; it is destined for you that, throughout your life, you will say: ‘Do not touch me’. And, of course, you have another promise that will not be broken for you. And look at your god to which you stayed devoted. We will certainly burn it, then we will scatter it thoroughly in the sea.
t.85: Moses said, ‘Get away from here! Your lot in this life is to say, “Do not touch me,” but you have an appointment from which there is no escape. Look at your god which you have kept on worshipping- we shall grind it down and scatter it into the sea.
t.95: Moses said: "Be gone, then. All your life you shall cry: 'Untouchable.' There awaits a term for your reckoning that you cannot fail to keep. Now look at your god that you devotedly adored: We shall burn it and scatter its remains in the sea.
t.19: (Moses) said: Then go! and lo! in this life it is for thee to say: Touch me not! and lo! there is for thee a tryst thou canst not break. Now look upon thy god of which thou hast remained a votary. Verily we will burn it and will scatter its dust over the sea.
t.22: (Moses) said: "Get thee gone! but thy (punishment) in this life will be that thou wilt say, 'touch me not'; and moreover (for a future penalty) thou hast a promise that will not fail: Now look at thy god, of whom thou hast become a devoted worshipper: We will certainly (melt) it in a blazing fire and scatter it broadcast in the sea!"
t.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said: "Then go away! And verily, your (punishment) in this life will be that you will say: "Touch me not (i.e. you will live alone exiled away from mankind); and verily (for a future torment), you have a promise that will not fail. And look at your ilâh (god) to which you have been devoted. We will certainly burn it, and scatter its particles in the sea."
t.54: کہا اچھا جا دنیا کی زندگی میں تیری سزا یہی ہے کہ تو کہتا رہے کہ مجھے نہ چھونا، اور ایک اور بھی وعده تیرے ساتھ ہے جو تجھ سے ہر گز نہ ٹلے گا، اور اب تو اپنے اس معبود کو بھی دیکھ لینا جس کا اعتکاف کیے ہوئے تھا کہ ہم اسے جلا کر دریا میں ریزه ریزه اڑا دیں گے.

t.149: Surely yourgod is none but Allah, the One besides Whom there is no other god; He has embraced everything in knowledge.
t.84: Your God is Allah other than whom there is no god. He encompasses everything with knowledge.”
t.85: [People], your true god is the One God- there is no god but Him- whose knowledge embraces everything.’
t.95: Your God is none else than Allah, beside Whom there is no god. His knowledge embraces everything."
t.19: Your Allah is only Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah. He embraceth all things in His knowledge.
t.22: But the god of you all is the One Allah: there is no god but He: all things He comprehends in His knowledge.
t.203: Your Ilâh (God) is only Allâh, (the One) Lâ ilâha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He). He has full knowledge of all things.
t.54: اصل بات یہی ہے کہ تم سب کا معبود برحق صرف اللہ ہی ہے اس کے سوا کوئی پرستش کے قابل نہیں۔ اس کا علم تمام چیزوں پر حاوی ہے.

t.149: Thus We narrate to youof the stories that have passed before, for We have brought you a Reminder from Us.
t.84: This is how We narrate to you certain events of what has passed, and We have given to you, from Ourself, a (book of) advice.
t.85: In this way We relate to you [Prophet] stories of what happened before. We have given you a Quran from Us.
t.95: (O Muhammad), thus do We recount to you the events of the past, and We have bestowed upon you from Ourself an admonition.
t.19: Thus relate We unto thee (Muhammad) some tidings of that which happened of old, and We have given thee from Our presence a reminder.
t.22: Thus do We relate to thee some stories of what happened before: for We have sent thee a Message from Our own Presence.
t.203: Thus We relate to you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) some information of what happened before. And indeed We have given you from Us a Reminder (this Qur’ân).
t.54: اسی طرح ہم تیرے سامنے پہلے کی گزری ہوئی وارداتیں بیان فرما رہے ہیں اور یقیناً ہم تجھے اپنے پاس سے نصیحت عطا فرما چکے ہیں.

t.149: Whoever has disregarded it will indeed carry on the Day of Resurrection a burden,
t.84: Whoever turns away from it shall certainly bear a heavy burden on Doomsday,
t.85: Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a heavy burden
t.95: He who turns away from it will surely bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection,
t.19: Whoso turneth away from it, he verily will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection,
t.22: If any do turn away therefrom, verily they will bear a burden on the Day of judgment;
t.203: Whoever turns away from it (this Qur’ân - i.e. does not believe in it, nor acts on its orders), verily, they will bear a heavy burden (of sins) on the Day of Resurrection,
t.54: اس سے جو منھ پھیر لے گا وه یقیناً قیامت کے دن اپنا بھاری بوجھ ﻻدے ہوئے ہوگا.

t.149: abidingin it, and how bad their load becameon the Day of Resurrection—
t.84: all such people living under it forever. And how evil for them will be that burden on the Doomsday!
t.85: and will remain under it. What a terrible burden to carry on that Day!
t.95: and will abide under this burden for ever. Grievous shall be the burden on the Day of Resurrection,
t.19: Abiding under it - an evil burden for them on the Day of Resurrection,
t.22: They will abide in this (state): and grievous will the burden be to them on that Day,-
t.203: They will abide in that (state in the Fire of Hell) - and evil indeed will it be that load for them on the Day of Resurrection;
t.54: جس میں ہمیشہ ہی رہے گا، اور ان کے لئے قیامت کے دن (بڑا) برا بوجھ ہے.

t.149: the day when the Trumpet is blown ! And We herd the criminals on that day, blue,
t.84: The Day when the Horn (Sūr) will be blown, and We shall gather them together while they will have turned blue on that day,
t.85: When the trumpet is sounded and We gather the sinful, sightless,
t.95: the Day when the Trumpet shall be sounded and We shall muster the sinners, their eyes turned blue with terror.
t.19: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror),
t.22: The Day when the Trumpet will be sounded: that Day, We shall gather the sinful, blear-eyed (with terror).
t.203: The Day when the Trumpet will be blown (the second blowing): that Day, We shall gather the Mujrimûn (criminals, polytheists, sinners, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allâh) blue or blind-eyed with thirst.
t.54: جس دن صور پھونکا جائے گا اور گناه گاروں کو ہم اس دن (دہشت کی وجہ سے) نیلی پیلی آنکھوں کے ساتھ گھیر ﻻئیں گے.

t.149: murmuring among themselves: “Youhave stayed only for ten.”
t.84: and will be whispering among themselves, “You did not remain (in graves) more than ten (days)”.
t.85: they will murmur to one another, ‘You stayed only ten days [on earth]’-
t.95: They shall whisper among themselves: "You stayed on the earth barely ten days."
t.19: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days).
t.22: In whispers will they consult each other: "Yet tarried not longer than ten (Days);
t.203: They will speak in a very low voice to each other (saying): "You stayed not longer than ten (days)."
t.54: وه آپس میں چپکے چپکے کہہ رہے ہوں گے کہ ہم تو (دنیا میں) صرف دس دن ہی رہے.

t.149: We know better what they say, when the most exemplary of them in conduct says, “Youhave stayed for no more than a day.”
t.84: We know very well what they say, when the best of them in his ways will say, “You did not remain more than one day.”
t.85: We know best what they say- but the more perceptive of them will say, ‘Your stay [on earth] was only a single day.’
t.95: We know well what they will say to one another: We also know that even the most cautious in his estimate will say: "You lived in the world no more than a day."
t.19: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day.
t.22: We know best what they will say, when their leader most eminent in conduct will say: "Ye tarried not longer than a day!"
t.203: We know very well what they will say, when the best among them in knowledge and wisdom will say: "You stayed no longer than a day!"
t.54: جوکچھ وه کہہ رہے ہیں اس کی حقیقت سے ہم باخبر ہیں ان میں سب سے زیاده اچھی راه واﻻ کہہ رہا ہو گا کہ تم تو صرف ایک ہی دن رہے.

t.149: And they ask you about the mountains. So say, “My Lord will blow them away
t.84: They ask you about the mountains. So, say (to them), “My Lord will crush them into dust thoroughly,
t.85: They ask you [Prophet] about the mountains: say, ‘[On that Day] my Lord will blast them into dust
t.95: They ask you concerning the mountains: "Where will they go?" Say: "My Lord will scatter them like dust,
t.19: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust.
t.22: They ask thee concerning the Mountains: say, "My Lord will uproot them and scatter them as dust;
t.203: And they ask you concerning the mountains: say, "My Lord will blast them and scatter them as particles of dust.
t.54: وه آپ سے پہاڑوں کی نسبت سوال کرتے ہیں، تو آپ کہہ دیں کہ انہیں میرا رب ریزه ریزه کر کے اڑا دے گا.

t.149: and leave them as desolate waste.
t.84: then will turn them into a leveled plain
t.85: and leave a flat plain,
t.95: and leave the earth a levelled plain
t.19: And leave it as an empty plain,
t.22: "He will leave them as plains smooth and level;
t.203: "Then He shall leave them as a level smooth plain.
t.54: اور زمین کو بالکل ہموار صاف میدان کر کے چھوڑے گا.

t.149: You will see in them neither crookedness nor deviation.”
t.84: in which you will see neither a curve nor an uneven place.”
t.85: with no peak or trough to be seen.
t.95: in which you shall find no crookedness or curvature.
t.19: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness.
t.22: "Nothing crooked or curved wilt thou see in their place."
t.203: "You will see therein nothing crooked or curved."
t.54: جس میں تو نہ کہیں موڑ دیکھے گا نہ اونچ نیچ.

t.149: On that day, they follow the caller without any crookedness, and voices were(hushed) in reverence to the All-Merciful, so that youhear nothing but a murmur.
t.84: That day they will follow the caller who will find no deviation (from anyone). And the voices will turn low in awe for the RaHmān (All-Merciful, Allah). So, you will hear not but whispering.
t.85: On that Day, people will follow the summoner from whom there is no escape; every voice will be hushed for the Lord of Mercy; only whispers will be heard.
t.95: On that Day people shall follow straight on to the call of the summoner, no one daring to show any haughtiness. Their voices shall be hushed before the Most Compassionate Lord, so that you will hear nothing but a whispering murmur.
t.19: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur.
t.22: On that Day will they follow the Caller (straight): no crookedness (can they show) him: all sounds shall humble themselves in the Presence of (Allah) Most Gracious: nothing shalt thou hear but the tramp of their feet (as they march).
t.203: On that Day mankind will follow strictly (the voice of) Allâh’s caller, no crookedness (that is without going to the right or left of that voice) will they show him (Allâh’s caller). And all voices will be humbled for the Most Gracious (Allâh), and nothing shall you hear but the low voice of their footsteps.
t.54: جس دن لوگ پکارنے والے کے پیچھے چلیں گے جس میں کوئی کجی نہ ہوگی اور اللہ رحمنٰ کے سامنے تمام آوازیں پست ہو جائیں گی سوائے کھسر پھسر کے تجھے کچھ بھی سنائی نہ دے گا.

t.149: On that day, intercession does not avail except for the one permitted by the All-Merciful, and He was pleased for him to speak.
t.84: That day no intercession will be of any use to anyone, except the one whom the RaHmān (All-Merciful, Allah) has permitted and was pleased with his word.
t.85: On that Day, intercession will be useless except from those to whom the Lord of Mercy has granted permission and whose words He approves-
t.95: On that Day intercession shall not avail save of him whom the Most Compassionate Lord permits, and whose word of intercession is pleasing to Him.
t.19: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth.
t.22: On that Day shall no intercession avail except for those for whom permission has been granted by (Allah) Most Gracious and whose word is acceptable to Him.
t.203: On that day no intercession shall avail, except the one for whom the Most Gracious (Allâh) has given permission and whose word is acceptable to Him.
t.54: اس دن سفارش کچھ کام نہیں آئے گی مگر جسے رحمنٰ حکم دے اور اس کی بات کو پسند فرمائے.

t.149: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot encompass Him with knowledge.
t.84: He knows what is in front of them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass Him in (their) knowledge.
t.85: He knows what is before and behind them, though they do not comprehend Him-
t.95: He knows all that is ahead of them and all that is behind them, while the others do not know.
t.19: He knoweth (all) that is before them and (all) that is behind them, while they cannot compass it in knowledge.
t.22: He knows what (appears to His creatures as) before or after or behind them: but they shall not compass it with their knowledge.
t.203: He (Allâh) knows what happens to them (His creatures) in this world, and what will happen to them (in the Hereafter) but they will never compass anything of His Knowledge.
t.54: جو کچھ ان کے آگے پیچھے ہے اسے اللہ ہی جانتا ہے مخلوق کا علم اس پر حاوی نہیں ہو سکتا.

t.149: And faces were humbledto the Living One, the All-Sustaining, and surely whoever carried injustice is bound to fail.
t.84: All faces will be humbled before (Allah,) the Ever-Alive, the All-Sustaining; and the loser will be the one who bears (the burden of his) injustice.
t.85: and [all] faces will be humbled before the Living, Ever Watchful One. Those burdened with evil deeds will despair,
t.95: All faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting Lord, and he who bears the burden of iniquity will have failed;
t.19: And faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. And he who beareth (a burden of) wrongdoing is indeed a failure (on that day).
t.22: (All) faces shall be humbled before (Him) - the Living, the Self-Subsisting, Eternal: hopeless indeed will be the man that carries iniquity (on his back).
t.203: And (all) faces shall be humbled before (Allâh), Al-Hayyul-Qayyum (the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists). And he who carried (a burden of) wrongdoing (i.e. he who disbelieved in Allâh, ascribed partners to Him, and did deeds of His disobedience), will be indeed a complete failure (on that Day).
t.54: تمام چہرے اس زنده اور قائم دائم مدبر، اللہ کے سامنے کمال عاجزی سے جھکے ہوئے ہونگے، یقیناً وه برباد ہوا جس نے ﻇلم ﻻد لیا.

t.149: But whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer, then he neither fears injustice nor curtailment.
t.84: But whoever does righteous deeds, while he is a believer, shall fear neither injustice nor curtailment (of his rewards).
t.85: but whoever has done righteous deeds and believed need have no fear of injustice or deprivation.’
t.95: but whosoever does righteous works, being a believer, shall have no fear of suffering wrong or loss."
t.19: And he who hath done some good works, being a believer, he feareth not injustice nor begrudging (of his wage).
t.22: But he who works deeds of righteousness, and has faith, will have no fear of harm nor of any curtailment (of what is his due).
t.203: And he who works deeds of righteousness, while he is a believer (in Islâmic Monotheism), then he will have no fear of injustice, nor of any curtailment (of his reward).
t.54: اور جو نیک اعمال کرے اور ایمان واﻻ بھی ہو تو نہ اسے بے انصافی کا کھٹکا ہوگا نہ حق تلفی کا.

t.149: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Recital, and We have diversified the warnings in it, that perhaps they would become mindful(of God) or it would bring about in them a remembrance.
t.84: And in this way We have sent it down to you as an Arabic Qur’ān, and have detailed in it some warnings in various ways, so that they may fear, or it may produce a lesson for them.
t.85: We have sent the Quran down in the Arabic tongue and given all kinds of warnings in it, so that they may beware or take heed-
t.95: (O Muhammad), thus have We revealed this as an Arabic Qur'an and have expounded in it warning in diverse ways so that they may avoid evil or become heedful.
t.19: Thus we have revealed it as a Lecture in Arabic, and have displayed therein certain threats, that peradventure they may keep from evil or that it may cause them to take heed.
t.22: Thus have We sent this down - an arabic Qur'an - and explained therein in detail some of the warnings, in order that they may fear Allah, or that it may cause their remembrance (of Him).
t.203: And thus We have sent it down as a Qur’ân in Arabic, and have explained therein in detail the warnings, in order that they may fear Allâh, or that it may cause them to have a lesson from it (or to have the honour for believing and acting on its teachings).
t.54: اسی طرح ہم نے تجھ پر عربی قرآن نازل فرمایا ہے اور طرح طرح سے اس میں ڈر کا بیان سنایا ہے تاکہ لوگ پرہیز گار بن جائیں یا ان کے دل میں سوچ سمجھ تو پیدا کرے.

t.149: Most high above all is Allah, the True King. Donot be hasty with the Recitalbefore its revelation to you is concluded , and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
t.84: So High above all is Allah, the True King! And do not hasten with (reciting) the Qur’ān before its revelation to you is concluded, and say, “My Lord, improve me in knowledge.”
t.85: exalted be God, the one who is truly in control. [Prophet], do not rush to recite before the revelation is fully complete but say, ‘Lord, increase me in knowledge!’
t.95: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Hasten not with reciting the Qur'an before its revelation to you is finished, and pray: "Lord! Increase me in knowledge."
t.19: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.
t.22: High above all is Allah, the King, the Truth! Be not in haste with the Qur'an before its revelation to thee is completed, but say, "O my Lord! advance me in knowledge."
t.203: Then High above all be Allâh, the True King. And be not in haste (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) with the Qur’ân before its revelation is completed to you, and say: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge."
t.54: پس اللہ عالی شان واﻻ سچا اور حقیقی بادشاه ہے۔ تو قرآن پڑھنے میں جلدی نہ کر اس سے پہلے کہ تیری طرف جو وحی کی جاتی ہے وه پوری کی جائے، ہاں یہ دعا کر کہ پروردگار! میرا علم بڑھا.

t.149: And most surely We covenanted with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no resolve.
t.84: We had given a directive to ’Ādam earlier, then he forgot, and We did not find in him a firm resolve.
t.85: We also commanded Adam before you, but he forgot and We found him lacking in constancy.
t.95: Most certainly We had given Adam a command before, but he forgot. We found him lacking in firmness of resolution.
t.19: And verily We made a covenant of old with Adam, but he forgot, and We found no constancy in him.
t.22: We had already, beforehand, taken the covenant of Adam, but he forgot: and We found on his part no firm resolve.
t.203: And indeed We made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found on his part no firm will-power.
t.54: ہم نے آدم کو پہلے ہی تاکیدی حکم دیا تھا لیکن وه بھول گیا اور ہم نے اس میں کوئی عزم نہیں پایا.

t.149: And recall when We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves to Adam.” So they prostrated themselves— but not Iblis; he refused.
t.84: When We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves to ’Ādam”. So, all of them fell prostrate, except Iblīs , who refused.
t.85: When We said to the angels, ‘Bow down before Adam,’ they did. But Iblis refused,
t.95: Recall when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves before Adam"; all prostrated themselves save Iblis. He refused.
t.19: And when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, they fell prostrate (all) save Iblis; he refused.
t.22: When We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves to Adam", they prostrated themselves, but not Iblis: he refused.
t.203: And (remember) when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves to Adam." They prostrated themselves (all) except Iblîs (Satan) he refused.
t.54: اور جب ہم نے فرشتوں سے کہا کہ آدم (علیہ السلام) کو سجده کرو تو ابلیس کے سوا سب نے کیا، اس نے صاف انکار کر دیا.

t.149: So We said, “O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your spouse. So do not let him get youout of the Garden, for then youwillsuffer.
t.84: So, We said “’Ādam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not expel you from Paradise, lest you should get into trouble.
t.85: so We said, ‘Adam, this is your enemy, yours and your wife’s: do not let him drive you out of the garden and make you miserable.
t.95: Then We said: "Adam! He is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not drive both of you out of Paradise and plunge you into affliction,
t.19: Therefor we said: O Adam! This is an enemy unto thee and unto thy wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden so that thou come to toil.
t.22: Then We said: "O Adam! verily, this is an enemy to thee and thy wife: so let him not get you both out of the Garden, so that thou art landed in misery.
t.203: Then We said: "O Adam! Verily, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not get you both out of Paradise, so that you will be distressed.
t.54: تو ہم نے کہا اے آدم! یہ تیرا اور تیری بیوی کا دشمن ہے (خیال رکھنا) ایسا نہ ہو کہ وه تم دونوں کو جنت سے نکلوا دے کہ تو مصیبت میں پڑ جائے.

t.149: In it, indeed, youwill never go hungry nor be naked.
t.84: Here you have the privilege that you will not be hungry nor will you be unclad,
t.85: In the garden you will never go hungry, feel naked,
t.95: (for in Paradise) neither are you hungry nor naked,
t.19: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked,
t.22: "There is therein (enough provision) for thee not to go hungry nor to go naked,
t.203: Verily, you have (a promise from Us) that you will never be hungry therein nor naked.
t.54: یہاں تو تجھے یہ آرام ہے کہ نہ تو بھوکا ہوتا ہے نہ ننگا.

t.149: Nor will you be thirsty in it nor will you swelter.”
t.84: and you will not be thirsty, nor will you be exposed to sun.”
t.85: be thirsty, or suffer the heat of the sun.’
t.95: nor face thirst or scorching heat."
t.19: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun's heat.
t.22: "Nor to suffer from thirst, nor from the sun's heat."
t.203: And you (will) suffer not from thirst therein nor from the sun’s heat.
t.54: اور نہ تو یہاں پیاسا ہوتا ہے نہ دھوپ سے تکلیف اٹھاتا ہے.

t.149: But Satan whispered to him. He said, “O Adam, shall I show you the Tree of Immortality and a kingdom that never decays?”
t.84: Then the Satan instigated him. He said, “’Ādam, shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and to an empire that does not decay?”
t.85: But Satan whispered to Adam, saying, ‘Adam, shall I show you the tree of immortality and power that never decays?’
t.95: But Satan seduced him, saying: "Adam! Shall I direct you to a tree of eternal life and an abiding kingdom?"
t.19: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away?
t.22: But Satan whispered evil to him: he said, "O Adam! shall I lead thee to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that never decays?"
t.203: Then Shaitân (Satan) whispered to him, saying: "O Adam! Shall I lead you to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that will never waste away?"
t.54: لیکن شیطان نے اسے وسوسہ ڈاﻻ، کہنے لگا کہ میں تجھے دائمی زندگی کا درخت اور بادشاہت بتلاؤں کہ جو کبھی پرانی نہ ہو.

t.149: So theyate from it, whereupon their private parts became exposed to them, and they started covering themselves with the leaves of the Garden. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and was deluded.
t.84: So, both of them Ādam and Hawwā’ (Eve)] ate from it, and their parts of shame were exposed to them, and they started stitching on themselves some of the leaves of Paradise. And ’Ādam disobeyed his Lord, and erred.
t.85: and they both ate from it. They became conscious of their nakedness and began to cover themselves with leaves from the garden. Adam disobeyed his Lord and was led astray-
t.95: Then the two of them ate the fruit of that tree and their shameful parts became revealed to each other, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves from the Garden. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and strayed into error.
t.19: Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray.
t.22: In the result, they both ate of the tree, and so their nakedness appeared to them: they began to sew together, for their covering, leaves from the Garden: thus did Adam disobey his Lord, and allow himself to be seduced.
t.203: Then they both ate of the tree, and so their private parts became manifest to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Paradise for their covering. Thus did Adam disobey his Lord, so he went astray.
t.54: چنانچہ ان دونوں نے اس درخت سے کچھ کھا لیا پس ان کے ستر کھل گئے اور بہشت کے پتے اپنے اوپر ٹانکنے لگے۔ آدم (علیہ السلام) نے اپنے رب کی نافرمانی کی، پس بہک گیا.

t.149: Then his Lord recalled him and granted him repentance and accepted it from him and guided(him) .
t.84: Thereafter his Lord chose him. So He accepted his repentance and gave (him) guidance.
t.85: later his Lord brought him close, accepted his repentance, and guided him-
t.95: Thereafter his Lord exalted him, accepted his repentance, and bestowed guidance upon him,
t.19: Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him.
t.22: But his Lord chose him (for His Grace): He turned to him, and gave him Guidance.
t.203: Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him with forgiveness, and gave him guidance.
t.54: پھر اس کے رب نے نوازا، اس کی توبہ قبول کی اور اس کی رہنمائی کی.

t.149: He said, “Descend from it, all together, some of you as enemies of some others. But whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.
t.84: He said (to ’Ādam and Iblīs), “Go down from here, all of you, some of you enemies of some others. Then, should some guidance come to you from Me, the one who follows My guidance shall not go astray, nor shall he be in trouble.
t.85: God said, ‘Get out of the garden as each other’s enemy.’ Whoever follows My guidance, when it comes to you [people], will not go astray nor fall into misery,
t.95: and said: "Get down, both of you, (that is, man and Satan), and be out of it; each of you shall be an enemy to the other. Henceforth if there comes to you a guidance from Me, then whosoever follows My guidance shall neither go astray nor suffer misery.
t.19: He said: Go down hence, both of you, one of you a foe unto the other. But when there come unto you from Me a guidance, then whoso followeth My guidance, he will not go astray nor come to grief.
t.22: He said: "Get ye down, both of you,- all together, from the Garden, with enmity one to another: but if, as is sure, there comes to you Guidance from Me, whosoever follows My Guidance, will not lose his way, nor fall into misery.
t.203: He (Allâh) said: "Get you down (from the Paradise to the earth), both of you, together, some of you are an enemy to some others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My Guidance he shall neither go astray, nor shall be distressed.
t.54: فرمایا، تم دونوں یہاں سےاتر جاؤ تم آپس میں ایک دوسرے کے دشمن ہو، اب تمہارے پاس کبھی میری طرف سے ہدایت پہنچے تو جو میری ہدایت کی پیروی کرے نہ تو وه بہکے گا نہ تکلیف میں پڑے گا.

t.149: But whoever has disregarded My Reminder—for him is a miserable life, and Wewill herd him on the Day of Resurrection blind.”
t.84: As for the one who turns away from My message, he shall have a straitened life, and We shall raise him blind on the Day of Judgment.”
t.85: but whoever turns away from it will have a life of great hardship. We shall bring him blind to the Assembly on the Day of Resurrection
t.95: But whosoever turns away from this Admonition from Me shall have a straitened life; We shall raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection,"
t.19: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection.
t.22: "But whosoever turns away from My Message, verily for him is a life narrowed down, and We shall raise him up blind on the Day of Judgment."
t.203: "But whosoever turns away from My Reminder (i.e. neither believes in this Qur’ân nor acts on its teachings.) verily, for him is a life of hardship, and We shall raise him up blind on the Day of Resurrection."
t.54: اور (ہاں) جو میری یاد سے روگردانی کرے گا اس کی زندگی تنگی میں رہے گی، اور ہم اسے بروز قیامت اندھا کر کے اٹھائیں گے.

t.149: He said, “My Lord, why did You herd me blind though I used to see?”
t.84: He will say, “My Lord, why did you raise me blind while I was sighted?”
